headline: Owerri Arts Workshop Series Faces Setback as COVID-19 Restrictions Limit Gatherings
summary: Plans for an arts workshop series in Owerri faced new challenges as COVID-19 restrictions limited public gatherings and disrupted cultural activities. Organisers and creative practitioners turned attention to preserving skills development and finding safer ways to keep participants engaged.
fullStory:
OWERRI — Plans for an arts workshop series in Owerri faced new challenges as measures to contain the spread of the coronavirus restricted public gatherings and disrupted cultural activities. The programme was expected to provide opportunities for artists and aspiring creatives to develop practical skills, but the emerging health crisis was making conventional workshops increasingly difficult to organise.

Cultural stakeholders said arts training remained important despite the disruption. They maintained that workshops could help young people and emerging artists develop skills in areas such as painting, crafts, performance, design and other creative disciplines. They urged organisers to preserve the programme while complying with public-health directives.

The restrictions on gatherings meant that organisers had to reconsider plans involving groups of participants working together in enclosed spaces. Stakeholders said postponement or smaller forms of engagement could be considered where appropriate, provided that such activities were consistent with official health guidance.

Artists and instructors were also facing financial difficulties as exhibitions, performances and other creative activities were being cancelled or postponed. Stakeholders said the interruption was affecting not only artists but also technicians, vendors, event workers and others whose incomes depended on the creative sector.

The workshop organisers were encouraged to maintain communication with participants and provide updates as the public-health situation developed. Stakeholders said clear information would help participants understand whether sessions had been postponed, modified or moved to alternative formats.

Digital platforms were identified as one possible way of continuing parts of the programme. Instructors could share tutorials, demonstrations and other learning materials online while physical workshops remained restricted. However, stakeholders acknowledged that limited internet access and the cost of data could make online participation difficult for some residents.

Community-based approaches could also provide opportunities for smaller-scale engagement when permitted. Stakeholders said any future physical workshops would need to take account of venue capacity, sanitation, crowd management and other health requirements.

The disruption highlighted the importance of supporting young creatives during periods of uncertainty. Stakeholders said many emerging artists depended on workshops and cultural programmes not only for training but also for networking and opportunities to display their work. They urged organisations to continue supporting participants even when normal activities could not proceed.

Arts practitioners also said the interruption could encourage greater use of digital tools in creative education. While online learning could not completely replace hands-on instruction in some disciplines, it could provide useful supplementary material and help artists remain connected with audiences and fellow practitioners.

Stakeholders called for cooperation between organisers, instructors, participants and community leaders. They said the programme's future would depend on the public-health situation and the restrictions in force at the time. Safety, they maintained, should remain the immediate priority.

As attention shifted towards practical planning, arts stakeholders in Owerri urged organisers to preserve the workshop programme and prepare for its eventual continuation. They said maintaining communication, supporting participants and exploring safe alternatives could help prevent the disruption from weakening local creative development.

The COVID-19 outbreak had created significant difficulties for the creative sector, but stakeholders maintained that arts education and skills development remained valuable. They expressed hope that the workshop series could resume when conditions allowed and provide artists in Owerri with renewed opportunities for training and collaboration.

headline: Abeokuta Reviews Transport Congestion Plan as COVID-19 Restrictions Alter Movement
summary: Transport stakeholders in Abeokuta reviewed measures for managing congestion as COVID-19 restrictions altered traffic patterns and passenger movement. Attention focused on keeping essential transport services operating while reducing unnecessary movement and protecting commuters.
fullStory:
ABEOKUTA — Transport stakeholders in Abeokuta reviewed measures for managing congestion as restrictions introduced to contain the spread of COVID-19 began altering traffic patterns and passenger movement. The changes were affecting commuters, commercial transport operators and businesses that depended on the regular movement of people and goods.

Stakeholders said the unusual reduction in normal movement presented both challenges and opportunities for transport management. While fewer commuters could ease congestion on some routes, restrictions and changes in travel patterns could also create difficulties at transport terminals and other points where essential passengers continued to gather.

Transport operators were urged to comply with official directives while maintaining essential services. Stakeholders said drivers and transport unions needed clear information about permitted operations, passenger limits and other requirements as authorities adjusted measures in response to the developing health situation.

Commuters were also encouraged to limit travel to essential activities where possible. Community leaders said unnecessary movement could increase health risks and urged residents to follow public-health guidance while planning their journeys.

The disruption was creating financial difficulties for commercial transport operators. Reduced passenger numbers meant lower earnings for many drivers and transport workers, while vehicle maintenance and operating expenses continued. Stakeholders called for practical support for operators whose livelihoods were being affected by the restrictions.

Businesses were similarly affected by changes in movement. Markets, shops and other commercial establishments depended on customers and workers being able to travel. Economic stakeholders said transport planning needed to consider the wider effect that restrictions could have on local commerce and household incomes.

Public-health precautions became an important part of the congestion discussion. Stakeholders urged operators and passengers to observe hygiene measures and avoid overcrowding at terminals and loading points. They said transport managers would need to monitor passenger movement and adjust arrangements where necessary.

The situation also highlighted the importance of coordination between transport authorities, security agencies and transport unions. Stakeholders said inconsistent enforcement or unclear instructions could create confusion for drivers and passengers. Regular communication, they maintained, would help ensure that transport operations remained orderly.

Some stakeholders said the temporary changes in traffic patterns could provide useful information for longer-term transport planning. Reduced movement offered an opportunity to observe routes, bottlenecks and areas where infrastructure improvements might eventually be required once normal activity returned.

Residents also called for attention to roads and other transport infrastructure. They said congestion was not solely the result of passenger volume and could be worsened by poor road conditions, inadequate traffic management and delays at busy junctions. Stakeholders urged authorities to consider these factors in future planning.

The pandemic was also changing the way people viewed public transportation. Stakeholders said future planning would need to consider the ability of transport systems to respond to health emergencies while maintaining access to essential services.

As attention shifted towards implementation, stakeholders in Abeokuta called for cooperation among transport operators, authorities and commuters. They said responsible movement, clear communication and proper observance of health measures would help manage traffic and reduce unnecessary risks during the disruption.

The COVID-19 outbreak had temporarily changed normal movement across Abeokuta, but stakeholders maintained that lessons from the period could contribute to better transport planning. They urged authorities to use the experience to identify weaknesses and prepare measures that could improve congestion management when regular economic and social activity eventually resumed.

headline: Ilorin Reviews Trade Corridor Upgrade as COVID-19 Disrupts Movement of Goods
summary: Economic stakeholders in Ilorin renewed attention on trade corridor improvements as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted the movement of goods and affected businesses. The focus was on keeping essential supply routes functional while improving transport and trade infrastructure for longer-term economic activity.
fullStory:
ILORIN — Economic stakeholders in Ilorin renewed attention on trade corridor improvements as the coronavirus outbreak disrupted the movement of goods and created new difficulties for businesses and traders. The disruption was affecting transportation, supply chains and access to markets as authorities introduced measures aimed at containing the spread of COVID-19.

Stakeholders said efficient trade corridors were important to the local economy because farmers, manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers depended on reliable routes to move goods. They maintained that improvements to roads, transport links and related infrastructure could reduce delays and costs while strengthening commercial activity.

The pandemic, however, was placing immediate pressure on existing trade networks. Restrictions on movement and changes in demand were affecting the movement of both agricultural products and manufactured goods. Stakeholders said essential supplies needed to continue moving while appropriate health measures were observed.

Transport operators reported difficulties caused by changing restrictions and reduced commercial activity. Stakeholders urged authorities to provide clear information about permitted movement and ensure that legitimate movement of essential goods was not unnecessarily disrupted.

Farmers and traders were particularly concerned about access to markets. Delays in transporting produce could result in losses, especially for perishable agricultural goods. Economic stakeholders called for better coordination between producers, transport operators and market authorities to reduce avoidable delays.

The disruption also increased operating costs for businesses. Longer travel times, uncertainty and reduced customer activity could make it more difficult for traders and manufacturers to maintain normal operations. Stakeholders said improved transport infrastructure would become even more important as businesses worked towards recovery.

Authorities and transport associations were encouraged to maintain clear communication with businesses. Stakeholders said traders needed reliable information about routes, restrictions and operating arrangements so that they could plan deliveries and manage inventories effectively.

The trade corridor discussion also highlighted the importance of infrastructure beyond roads. Stakeholders said storage facilities, markets, transport terminals and other logistics infrastructure formed part of an effective trade network. Improvements in these areas could help reduce losses and make local businesses more competitive.

The pandemic also demonstrated the vulnerability of supply chains to sudden disruptions. Stakeholders said future trade corridor planning should include contingency measures that would allow essential goods to continue moving during emergencies while protecting workers and communities.

Business representatives called for support for small and medium-sized enterprises affected by the disruption. They said access to affordable finance and practical assistance could help businesses maintain operations and retain workers until commercial activity improved.

Stakeholders also encouraged stronger links between local producers and markets. They said improving domestic supply chains could reduce dependence on distant sources and help local businesses respond more effectively when external trade routes were disrupted.

As attention shifted towards implementation, economic stakeholders in Ilorin called for practical measures to improve trade routes and maintain essential movement during the crisis. They said better coordination, reliable infrastructure and clear operating guidance would help businesses manage the immediate disruption while preparing for future growth.

The COVID-19 outbreak had created significant challenges for trade and transportation, but stakeholders maintained that the period reinforced the importance of developing stronger trade corridors. They urged authorities to continue planning improvements that could reduce logistics costs, protect supply chains and support economic recovery when normal activity resumed.

headline: Jos Live Music Tour Put on Hold as COVID-19 Restrictions Halt Gatherings
summary: Plans for a live music tour in Jos were disrupted as COVID-19 restrictions on public gatherings affected concerts and other entertainment activities. Musicians, organisers and industry stakeholders turned attention to preserving the sector and preparing for the eventual return of live performances.
fullStory:
JOS — Plans for a live music tour in Jos were disrupted as measures introduced to contain the spread of COVID-19 restricted public gatherings and brought live entertainment activities to a halt. The development affected musicians, event organisers, venue operators and other workers whose livelihoods depended on concerts and related activities.

Stakeholders said live music remained an important part of the city's entertainment scene, providing opportunities for performers to reach audiences while supporting a wider network of workers. However, they acknowledged that organising concerts during the emerging health crisis could expose audiences and performers to unnecessary risks.

Organisers were urged to comply with official directives and postpone large gatherings where restrictions applied. Stakeholders said protecting public health had to take priority, even though postponements could result in financial losses for performers and event organisers who had already invested in preparations.

Musicians and other creative practitioners were facing growing financial pressure as concerts, festivals and other public events were cancelled or postponed. Many performers depended on live appearances for income, while technicians, sound engineers, security workers, vendors and transport operators also relied on entertainment events for their livelihoods.

Stakeholders called for greater support for creative workers affected by the disruption. They said assistance, where available, should be accessible to practitioners across the entertainment sector, including independent artists who might not have formal business structures or regular financial reserves.

The interruption also encouraged discussion about alternative ways of engaging music audiences. Stakeholders said artists could use radio, social media and other digital platforms to maintain contact with fans while physical performances remained restricted. Online performances and recorded content could provide some opportunities for artists to remain active, although they could not fully replace the income and atmosphere of live concerts.

Organisers were also encouraged to maintain communication with artists and ticket holders. Clear information about postponements, cancellations and future dates would help reduce uncertainty and allow participants to plan accordingly.

The crisis highlighted the importance of the wider creative economy in Jos. Live music events supported more than performers alone, creating temporary employment for event planners, photographers, decorators, caterers, technicians and other service providers. Stakeholders said the disruption could therefore have a broader economic effect than the cancellation of individual concerts suggested.

Health and safety requirements were expected to remain important when live entertainment eventually resumed. Stakeholders said organisers would need to consider venue capacity, sanitation, crowd management and other public-health measures before returning to large-scale concerts.

The situation also prompted some practitioners to consider longer-term changes to the way live music was organised. Stakeholders said stronger digital promotion, better event planning and more flexible approaches could help the sector become more resilient to future disruptions.

As attention shifted towards implementation and planning, entertainment stakeholders in Jos urged artists and organisers to remain patient and comply with public-health directives. They said preserving the health of audiences and performers was essential to creating the conditions for the eventual return of live entertainment.

The COVID-19 outbreak had created an unprecedented interruption for the entertainment industry, but stakeholders maintained that live music would remain an important part of Jos's cultural life. They called for continued support for practitioners and careful preparation so that concerts and music tours could resume safely when conditions permitted.

headline: Kaduna Reviews Community Market Operations as COVID-19 Restrictions Take Effect
summary: Community leaders and market stakeholders in Kaduna reviewed market operations as COVID-19 restrictions disrupted trading activities and changed how residents accessed essential goods. Attention focused on maintaining food supplies while improving sanitation, crowd management and public-health compliance.
fullStory:
KADUNA — Community leaders and market stakeholders in Kaduna reviewed market operations as measures introduced to contain the spread of COVID-19 disrupted trading activities and changed how residents accessed essential goods. The situation placed new pressure on traders, consumers and local authorities to maintain essential supplies while reducing the risk of transmission in crowded market environments.

Markets remained important to households that depended on them for food and other basic necessities. Stakeholders said any measures affecting market operations needed to balance public-health concerns with the need to ensure that residents could continue to obtain essential goods.

The restrictions were also creating difficulties for traders. Reduced customer traffic and changes in opening arrangements were affecting daily earnings, particularly for small traders who depended on regular sales. Market representatives called for clear guidance on permitted trading activities so that traders could plan their operations.

Crowd management became a major concern. Stakeholders said markets could become points of increased exposure if large numbers of people gathered without appropriate precautions. They urged traders and customers to observe official health guidance and avoid unnecessary crowding where possible.

Sanitation was also receiving increased attention. Market leaders encouraged regular cleaning of trading areas and proper disposal of waste. Traders and customers were urged to maintain good hygiene practices, including frequent handwashing and other precautions recommended by health authorities.

The disruption also affected the movement of food and other goods into Kaduna markets. Transport restrictions and changes in commercial activity could delay deliveries and increase costs. Stakeholders said coordination between transport operators, traders and market authorities would be necessary to keep essential supplies moving.

Consumers were encouraged to avoid panic buying. Community leaders said purchasing excessive quantities of goods could place additional pressure on households with limited resources and make shortages more likely. They urged residents to buy according to their needs and follow official information about market availability.

The situation highlighted the importance of supporting vulnerable households. Residents who depended on daily earnings could face difficulties meeting basic needs when market activity was disrupted. Stakeholders called for community support and appropriate assistance for families most affected by the restrictions.

Market associations were encouraged to communicate changes in trading arrangements to their members. Clear information about opening times, permitted activities and health requirements could help reduce confusion and improve compliance.

The crisis also prompted discussion about longer-term improvements to market infrastructure. Stakeholders said better sanitation facilities, improved waste management, wider access points and more organised trading spaces could make markets safer and more resilient during future emergencies.

As attention shifted towards implementation, stakeholders in Kaduna called for practical cooperation between market associations, residents and authorities. They said maintaining essential supplies, improving sanitation and managing crowds would be critical while public-health restrictions remained in place.

The COVID-19 outbreak had disrupted normal commercial activity, but stakeholders maintained that the experience could provide an opportunity to improve the organisation and resilience of community markets. They urged authorities and market leaders to use the period to strengthen systems that would protect traders and consumers while keeping essential goods available.

headline: Enugu Expands Sanitation Campaign as COVID-19 Raises Public Health Concerns
summary: Community leaders and health stakeholders in Enugu expanded sanitation awareness as the COVID-19 outbreak heightened concerns about hygiene and disease prevention. The campaign focused on encouraging residents to maintain cleaner surroundings and follow recommended public-health practices.
fullStory:
ENUGU — Community leaders and health stakeholders in Enugu expanded sanitation awareness as the COVID-19 outbreak heightened concerns about hygiene and disease prevention. The campaign focused on encouraging residents to maintain cleaner surroundings and adopt recommended public-health practices as authorities intensified efforts to limit the spread of the virus.

Stakeholders said good sanitation was an important part of protecting communities during the health emergency. They urged residents to pay greater attention to personal hygiene, household cleanliness and the proper disposal of waste, particularly in densely populated areas where poor sanitation could create additional health risks.

Community leaders encouraged residents to maintain regular handwashing and follow other guidance issued by health authorities. They said simple preventive measures could help reduce the risk of infection when consistently practised by individuals and households.

Waste management was another area of concern. Stakeholders said improperly disposed refuse could create unsanitary conditions and make public spaces more difficult to manage. Residents were urged to use designated waste disposal points and avoid dumping refuse in drains, roadsides and other unauthorised locations.

The campaign also drew attention to public spaces. Markets, transport areas and other locations where residents might still gather for essential activities required additional attention to cleanliness. Stakeholders called for regular cleaning and appropriate hygiene facilities where feasible.

Health workers and community representatives said accurate information was essential to the success of the campaign. They urged residents to rely on information from recognised health authorities rather than rumours or unverified claims about COVID-19 prevention.

The economic disruption caused by the pandemic was also affecting sanitation activities. Local businesses and households were facing financial pressure, while authorities and community organisations had to manage limited resources. Stakeholders called for cooperation between residents, businesses and local authorities to maintain basic sanitation standards despite the difficult circumstances.

Community organisations were encouraged to support vulnerable households. Stakeholders said elderly residents and families facing financial difficulties might require additional assistance in accessing water, hygiene supplies and other basic necessities.

The campaign also highlighted the importance of protecting sanitation workers. Stakeholders said workers responsible for collecting waste and maintaining public spaces needed appropriate protection and clear guidance while carrying out their duties during the health emergency.

Schools and other institutions that remained closed were also expected to maintain sanitation standards on their premises where necessary. Stakeholders said proper cleaning and preparation would be important before facilities eventually reopened.

Residents were further encouraged to avoid practices that could increase health risks, including unnecessary gatherings and careless disposal of protective materials. Community leaders said responsible behaviour was necessary to complement official efforts to contain the outbreak.

As attention shifted towards implementation, stakeholders in Enugu called for sustained sanitation efforts rather than short-term campaigns. They said maintaining clean surroundings, improving waste disposal and promoting good hygiene could provide benefits beyond the immediate COVID-19 emergency.

The outbreak had increased public attention on sanitation and disease prevention across the country. Stakeholders maintained that stronger community participation would be essential to keeping Enugu's neighbourhoods clean and supporting broader public-health efforts during the crisis.

headline: Benin City Reviews Small Business Support as COVID-19 Disrupts Economic Activity
summary: Business stakeholders in Benin City reviewed support measures for small enterprises as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted trading, services and household incomes. Attention focused on helping businesses survive the slowdown while protecting jobs and preparing for economic recovery.
fullStory:
BENIN CITY — Business stakeholders in Benin City reviewed support measures for small enterprises as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted trading, services and other economic activities. Small businesses were among those facing reduced customer demand, movement restrictions and difficulties meeting operating costs as efforts to contain the virus affected normal commercial activity.

Stakeholders said small and medium-sized businesses played an important role in the local economy because they provided employment and essential goods and services to residents. They maintained that protecting viable businesses during the disruption would be important to preserving jobs and supporting recovery when restrictions were eventually eased.

Traders and business owners reported difficulties caused by reduced customer traffic and interruptions to normal operations. Businesses that depended on daily sales were particularly exposed because a prolonged slowdown could quickly affect their ability to pay workers, rent and suppliers.

Stakeholders called for practical support that would help businesses manage the immediate pressure. Possible areas of assistance included access to affordable financing, temporary relief on certain operating costs and clearer information about available government programmes.

The movement restrictions were also affecting supply chains. Some businesses faced difficulties obtaining goods from suppliers or transporting products to customers. Stakeholders said maintaining essential supply routes would help reduce shortages and limit additional costs for businesses and consumers.

Financial institutions were encouraged to work with affected businesses where possible. Stakeholders said temporary repayment arrangements and accessible financing could provide breathing space for enterprises experiencing a sharp decline in revenue. They also urged business owners to maintain accurate records to help them assess their needs and access legitimate support.

Small businesses were also encouraged to adapt their operations where possible. Some traders and service providers were exploring delivery arrangements, digital communication and other methods of reaching customers while complying with public-health requirements. Stakeholders said such adaptations could help businesses remain connected to customers during the disruption.

The crisis was placing additional pressure on workers as businesses reduced hours or temporarily suspended operations. Stakeholders said support measures should consider employees as well as business owners because household incomes were closely linked to the survival of local enterprises.

Community organisations also highlighted the importance of supporting vulnerable businesses. Informal traders and very small enterprises could have limited access to formal financial services, making them particularly vulnerable to prolonged disruption. Stakeholders called for support programmes that were simple, transparent and accessible to businesses operating at different levels.

The situation also prompted discussion about the need for stronger business resilience. Stakeholders said enterprises could benefit from better financial planning, diversified supply arrangements and greater use of digital tools once economic activity began to recover.

Authorities and business associations were encouraged to maintain regular communication. Stakeholders said entrepreneurs needed reliable information about restrictions, available assistance and changes to commercial regulations so they could make informed decisions.

As attention shifted towards implementation, stakeholders in Benin City called for coordinated support between government agencies, financial institutions, business associations and individual enterprises. They said timely assistance could help prevent temporary disruption from becoming permanent business closures.

The COVID-19 outbreak had created significant economic uncertainty, but stakeholders maintained that supporting small businesses would be essential to recovery. They urged authorities to continue reviewing conditions and strengthen measures that could protect enterprises, preserve jobs and help the local economy return to normal activity when circumstances allowed.

headline: Port Harcourt Revives Local Council Accountability Drive Amid COVID-19 Disruptions
summary: Political and civic stakeholders in Port Harcourt renewed calls for stronger accountability at the local council level as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted normal public activities. Attention focused on transparency, responsible management of public resources and keeping residents informed during the emergency.
fullStory:
PORT HARCOURT — Political and civic stakeholders in Port Harcourt renewed calls for stronger accountability at the local council level as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted normal public activities and placed additional pressure on government institutions. Stakeholders said local authorities needed to maintain transparency and responsible management of public resources while responding to the demands created by the health emergency.

The outbreak had affected the way residents interacted with public institutions, with restrictions on movement and gatherings limiting conventional meetings and community engagements. Stakeholders said these limitations should not prevent councils from communicating decisions and providing residents with information about programmes and expenditure.

Civic representatives said accountability was particularly important during an emergency because public institutions could be required to redirect resources towards health, sanitation and other urgent needs. They urged local authorities to ensure that spending decisions were properly documented and communicated through accessible channels.

The response to the pandemic was also increasing demand for essential services. Residents were looking to government agencies for information about health measures, sanitation activities and assistance for vulnerable households. Stakeholders said councils needed effective systems for identifying local needs and responding to them within available resources.

Community leaders called for regular communication between councils and residents. They said public statements, radio announcements and other accessible platforms could help residents understand government decisions at a time when large public meetings were restricted.

The disruption also created concerns about the ability of residents to monitor local government activities. Traditional forms of public oversight were becoming more difficult because of restrictions on movement and gatherings. Civic stakeholders therefore encouraged councils to make relevant information available through alternative channels.

Stakeholders also emphasised the importance of protecting public resources from misuse. They said emergency circumstances should not weaken established procedures for procurement, record keeping and financial reporting. Where urgent action was necessary, they maintained that proper documentation remained important for later review.

The situation placed additional pressure on local officials to balance competing demands. Councils were expected to support public-health efforts while continuing essential administrative functions. Stakeholders said clear priorities and transparent decision-making would help maintain public confidence during the disruption.

Political organisations and community groups were encouraged to approach the situation responsibly. Stakeholders warned against using the health crisis to spread unverified allegations or create unnecessary political tension. They said legitimate criticism should be based on evidence and directed through appropriate channels.

The crisis also highlighted the potential role of technology in public accountability. Where infrastructure allowed, councils could use websites, social media and other digital platforms to publish announcements and provide updates on programmes. Stakeholders acknowledged, however, that not all residents had equal access to digital services.

As attention shifted towards implementation, civic and political stakeholders in Port Harcourt called for continued oversight despite the restrictions. They said transparency, accurate communication and proper documentation would help ensure that emergency resources were used responsibly and that residents remained informed.

The COVID-19 outbreak had created unusual challenges for local governance, but stakeholders maintained that accountability should remain a central responsibility. They urged local councils to strengthen communication with residents and preserve transparent administrative practices while responding to the immediate demands of the health emergency.

headline: Ibadan Creative Industry Summit Postponed as COVID-19 Restrictions Halt Gatherings
summary: Plans for a creative industry summit in Ibadan were disrupted as COVID-19 restrictions on public gatherings affected events across the city. Stakeholders said the creative sector had an important role in the local economy, providing employment and income for performers, technicians, designers, event workers and other practitioners. However, the health emergency was forcing many organisations to postpone meetings and reconsider activities that required large numbers of people to gather.

Organisers were urged to comply with public-health directives and avoid holding the summit while restrictions on gatherings remained in place. Stakeholders said protecting participants and the wider public had to take priority over the immediate continuation of industry events.

The postponement was also expected to affect discussions that could have provided opportunities for collaboration and business development. Creative practitioners said the sector needed platforms where artists and industry professionals could exchange ideas, identify opportunities and address challenges affecting their work.

Concerts, exhibitions, film productions, cultural events and other activities had been postponed or cancelled, reducing income for people who depended on the creative economy. Stakeholders called for greater attention to the financial difficulties facing independent practitioners.

Industry representatives said digital platforms could provide an alternative means of maintaining communication. Online meetings, webinars and social-media discussions could allow some of the conversations planned for the summit to continue without requiring a physical gathering. However, stakeholders acknowledged that limited internet access and the cost of data could restrict participation.

The crisis also encouraged creative organisations to consider new approaches to business. Stakeholders said practitioners could make greater use of digital distribution, online promotion and remote collaboration while conventional events remained restricted. They noted that these approaches could remain useful even after normal activities resumed.

Participants also stressed the importance of supporting emerging creatives. Many young artists and entrepreneurs relied on events, workshops and industry networks to gain exposure and develop professional relationships. As attention shifted towards practical alternatives, industry stakeholders in Ibadan urged organisers to maintain contact with participants and preserve the objectives of the summit. They said postponement should not mean abandoning discussions about investment, skills development, employment and other issues affecting the creative economy.

They expressed hope that the summit could eventually take place when public-health conditions permitted, while encouraging practitioners to use available platforms to remain connected and continue developing the sector.

headline: Lagos Reviews Public Wi-Fi Rollout as COVID-19 Disrupts Daily Life
summary: Authorities and technology stakeholders in Lagos reviewed public Wi-Fi plans as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted schools, businesses and other daily activities. Attention focused on improving access to reliable internet services for residents increasingly dependent on digital communication.
fullStory:
LAGOS — Authorities and technology stakeholders in Lagos reviewed plans to expand public Wi-Fi access as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted schools, businesses and other daily activities. The increased reliance on digital communication was drawing attention to the importance of affordable and reliable internet access for residents across the city.

The closure of schools and restrictions on public gatherings were pushing more activities online. Students, workers, businesses and community organisations were increasingly using digital platforms to communicate, learn and maintain contact while normal activities remained disrupted.

Stakeholders said public Wi-Fi could help residents who could not afford regular data subscriptions or did not have reliable internet connections at home. They maintained that wider access could support education, access to information and communication during the health emergency.

However, stakeholders said any public Wi-Fi rollout would need to consider network reliability, coverage and security. They called for proper planning to ensure that facilities were accessible in areas where demand was high and that users could connect without unnecessary difficulties.

The digital divide remained a major concern. While some households had smartphones, computers and reliable internet connections, others had limited access to devices or could not regularly afford data. Stakeholders said expanding public connectivity would be useful but should form part of a wider effort to improve digital inclusion.

Education was one of the areas where internet access was becoming increasingly important. With schools closed, students and teachers were exploring online learning and other remote methods of maintaining educational activities. Stakeholders said affordable connectivity could make it easier for more students to participate in such programmes.

Small businesses were also relying more heavily on digital tools. Traders and service providers were using messaging applications and social media to communicate with customers, promote products and arrange deliveries. Stakeholders said better connectivity could help businesses adapt to changing conditions.

Public information was another important consideration. Residents needed access to accurate information about COVID-19 restrictions, health guidance and government announcements. Stakeholders said reliable internet access could complement radio and other traditional media by giving residents additional ways to obtain official information.

The rollout also raised questions about maintenance and sustainability. Stakeholders said public Wi-Fi infrastructure would require regular maintenance, adequate bandwidth and reliable power supplies. Without proper management, they warned, services could become unreliable or deteriorate after installation.

Security and responsible use were also highlighted. Operators would need to protect users from common online risks while ensuring that public networks were not abused. Stakeholders encouraged residents to take basic precautions when using shared networks, particularly when accessing sensitive information.

Technology stakeholders said the increased dependence on digital communication during the pandemic could have longer-term effects. They maintained that habits developed during the crisis, including remote learning, online commerce and digital communication, could continue after normal activities resumed.

As attention shifted towards implementation, stakeholders in Lagos called for practical measures to expand reliable and affordable connectivity. They said public Wi-Fi could support residents during the disruption if it was properly planned, maintained and made accessible to communities with limited internet options.

The COVID-19 outbreak had accelerated the need for digital access across many areas of daily life. Stakeholders maintained that improving connectivity could help households, students and businesses manage the immediate disruption while laying a stronger foundation for wider digital participation in the future.

headline: Kano Night Market Festival Suspended as COVID-19 Restrictions Take Effect
summary: Plans for a night market festival in Kano were suspended as COVID-19 restrictions on public gatherings and movement disrupted entertainment and commercial activities. Stakeholders said the interruption demonstrated the vulnerability of creative workers whose livelihoods depended heavily on physical gatherings.

Community leaders also welcomed the emphasis on public safety. They urged residents to avoid unnecessary gatherings and follow health guidance issued by relevant authorities. Stakeholders said protecting public health should remain the priority until conditions allowed larger events to resume safely.

The disruption prompted organisers to consider alternative ways of maintaining interest in the festival. Digital promotion, recorded performances and online cultural activities could help keep the event visible while physical gatherings remained restricted. Stakeholders acknowledged, however, that such alternatives could not fully replace the commercial and social benefits of a live night market.

Food vendors and other small businesses were encouraged to consider safe ways of serving customers where permitted. Stakeholders said businesses that remained operational needed to follow applicable health and safety requirements and avoid creating unnecessary crowding.

Cultural representatives stressed that the event could also support local traditions and creative expression. A successful night market could provide opportunities for artisans and performers to showcase locally produced goods and cultural content while attracting visitors to the city.

The wider entertainment industry was facing similar disruptions as concerts, festivals and other public events were cancelled or postponed across Nigeria. Stakeholders said support for creative workers and small businesses would be important as the sector dealt with the effects of the pandemic.

As attention shifted towards implementation and future planning, organisers in Kano urged participants to remain patient and follow official health directives. They said maintaining communication with traders, performers and residents would help ensure that the festival could return when conditions permitted.

The COVID-19 outbreak had created significant challenges for entertainment and small-scale commerce, but stakeholders maintained that the night market festival remained viable as a future cultural and economic event. headline: Abuja Expands Public Wi-Fi Access as COVID-19 Drives Demand for Digital Services
summary: Authorities and technology stakeholders in Abuja expanded attention on public Wi-Fi access as the COVID-19 pandemic increased reliance on digital communication, online learning and remote work. The initiative was expected to help residents who faced difficulties accessing affordable and reliable internet services.
fullStory:
ABUJA — Authorities and technology stakeholders in Abuja expanded attention on public Wi-Fi access as the COVID-19 pandemic increased reliance on digital communication, online learning and remote work. The shift was creating greater demand for affordable and reliable internet services as schools, businesses and other institutions adapted to restrictions on normal activities.

Stakeholders said improved public connectivity could help residents stay informed and maintain access to essential digital services during the disruption. They noted that students, workers and small businesses were increasingly dependent on internet access to continue their activities while physical interaction remained limited.

The closure of schools was one of the major factors increasing demand for digital services. Students and teachers were turning to online platforms and other remote learning methods to maintain educational activities. Stakeholders said public Wi-Fi could provide an important option for students who did not have reliable internet access at home.

Small businesses were also exploring digital methods to remain connected with customers. Traders and service providers were using social media and messaging platforms to promote products, communicate with customers and arrange transactions. Better connectivity could make these adjustments easier for businesses facing reduced physical activity.

Stakeholders, however, said expanding public Wi-Fi would require careful planning. Coverage, network capacity and reliability would need to be considered to ensure that the service could meet demand in areas where large numbers of residents might depend on it.

The digital divide remained a significant concern. Some households had access to smartphones and broadband services, while others faced difficulties purchasing data or obtaining suitable devices. Stakeholders said public connectivity should therefore be developed alongside broader measures to improve digital inclusion.

Public information was another important consideration. Residents needed timely access to official announcements about COVID-19 restrictions, health advice and essential services. Stakeholders said reliable internet access could complement radio and television by giving residents another way to obtain verified information.

Technology experts also highlighted the need for proper maintenance. Public Wi-Fi infrastructure would require reliable power, sufficient bandwidth, regular technical support and security measures. Without sustained investment, stakeholders warned that connectivity projects could become unreliable after their initial launch.

Cybersecurity and responsible use were also raised. Operators would need to protect public networks from misuse while users should take precautions when accessing sensitive accounts through shared connections. Stakeholders encouraged residents to follow basic online security practices.

The increased use of digital services during the pandemic was also expected to have longer-term effects. Stakeholders said habits developed during the crisis, including remote work, online learning and digital commerce, could remain important even after restrictions were lifted.

As attention shifted towards implementation, technology and community stakeholders in Abuja called for practical steps to expand affordable connectivity. They said public Wi-Fi could help reduce the digital gap and provide residents with greater access to education, information and economic opportunities during the disruption.

The pandemic had accelerated the need for reliable internet access across many parts of society. Stakeholders maintained that expanding public connectivity could help Abuja residents manage the immediate challenges created by COVID-19 while supporting broader digital development in the years ahead.

headline: Yola State Assembly Reviews Key Policies as COVID-19 Disrupts Legislative Activities
summary: Lawmakers and political stakeholders in Yola reviewed key policy issues as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted normal legislative activities and public gatherings. Attention focused on maintaining effective oversight while adapting legislative work to the health emergency.
fullStory:
YOLA — Lawmakers and political stakeholders in Yola reviewed key policy issues as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted normal legislative activities and public gatherings. The health emergency was creating new challenges for lawmakers as restrictions on movement and gatherings affected conventional legislative meetings and consultations.

Stakeholders said the state assembly remained important to the functioning of government despite the disruption. They maintained that lawmakers needed to continue considering issues affecting residents while observing directives introduced to limit the spread of the virus.

The pandemic was placing new demands on government institutions. Health, sanitation and emergency response had become immediate priorities, while households and businesses were also facing economic difficulties. Stakeholders said legislative attention would need to reflect these changing circumstances.

Public consultations were among the activities affected by restrictions on gatherings. Lawmakers normally relied on meetings with constituents, community representatives and other stakeholders to understand local concerns. The disruption made such engagements more difficult, prompting calls for alternative channels of communication.

Political stakeholders encouraged lawmakers to maintain contact with constituents through available platforms. Radio broadcasts, telephone communication and digital channels could provide opportunities for residents to raise concerns and receive updates while physical meetings remained restricted.

Oversight was another important issue. Stakeholders said the emergency response involved public resources that needed to be managed responsibly. They urged lawmakers to maintain appropriate scrutiny of government spending and programmes while recognising the need for timely action during the crisis.

The economic impact of the pandemic was also expected to influence legislative discussions. Businesses were experiencing reduced activity, workers faced income uncertainty and households were adjusting to restrictions on movement. Stakeholders said lawmakers needed to consider measures that could support economic recovery and protect vulnerable residents.

Health and public safety remained central to the discussions. Stakeholders urged lawmakers to support efforts to improve public awareness, sanitation and access to essential services. They said legislative decisions should complement wider efforts to contain the spread of COVID-19.

The disruption also highlighted the importance of clear communication between government institutions and the public. Residents needed reliable information about restrictions, government programmes and emergency measures. Stakeholders called on lawmakers and other officials to communicate decisions promptly and avoid creating unnecessary uncertainty.

Political actors were also urged to avoid using the health emergency to deepen political tensions. Stakeholders said disagreements over policy were part of democratic processes, but public debate needed to remain responsible during a period when residents were already facing significant health and economic concerns.

The crisis could also encourage the assembly to consider more flexible approaches to legislative work. Where permitted, digital communication and smaller consultations could help maintain some activities while reducing health risks. Stakeholders said any changes would need to remain consistent with applicable rules and official health guidance.

As attention shifted towards implementation, political stakeholders in Yola called for continued legislative engagement and oversight despite the disruption. They said lawmakers needed to remain responsive to residents while adapting their methods of work to the changing public-health environment.

The COVID-19 outbreak had created an unusual challenge for government institutions, but stakeholders maintained that effective representation and accountability remained important. They urged the state assembly and political stakeholders to work together responsibly while keeping the interests and safety of residents at the centre of their response.

headline: Bauchi Backs Regional Cooperation on COVID-19 Response and Economic Recovery
summary: Political and community stakeholders in Bauchi backed stronger regional cooperation as the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted movement, trade and household incomes. Attention focused on coordinating public-health measures while protecting essential supplies and supporting economic recovery.
fullStory:
BAUCHI — Political and community stakeholders in Bauchi backed stronger regional cooperation as the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted movement, trade and household incomes. Stakeholders said cooperation among neighbouring states and relevant institutions would be important in managing the health emergency and limiting its wider economic effects.

The pandemic was affecting communities across state boundaries, making coordination particularly important for public-health officials, transport operators, traders and other groups whose activities depended on movement between different areas. Stakeholders said inconsistent measures could create confusion and make it more difficult to maintain essential services.

Political representatives called for greater communication between authorities responsible for managing the response. They said information about movement restrictions, health precautions and essential services needed to be shared clearly so that residents and businesses could make informed decisions.

The movement of food and other essential goods was another major concern. Restrictions introduced to slow transmission were affecting supply chains and creating difficulties for traders and transport operators. Stakeholders said essential goods should continue to move while appropriate health and safety measures were observed.

Households were also facing increasing economic pressure. Many workers and small businesses had experienced reduced income as commercial activities slowed. Community leaders urged authorities to consider the needs of vulnerable families when designing relief and recovery measures.

Small businesses and informal workers were particularly exposed to the disruption. Traders, artisans and other workers who depended on daily activity could quickly lose income when movement was restricted. Stakeholders called for practical assistance and easier access to legitimate support programmes.

The health response remained central to the discussions. Stakeholders urged residents to observe official guidance on hygiene, physical distancing and movement. They said cooperation between communities and authorities would help reduce the risk of transmission while allowing essential activities to continue.

Regional cooperation was also seen as important for information sharing. Stakeholders said authorities could learn from measures adopted in neighbouring areas and coordinate responses where communities and supply routes crossed administrative boundaries.

The crisis further highlighted the importance of transport links. Restrictions had reduced normal passenger movement, while traders still needed reliable routes for essential goods. Stakeholders called for clear procedures that would allow necessary commercial transportation to continue without undermining public-health measures.

Political and community leaders also emphasised the need for responsible public communication. They warned that rumours and unverified reports could increase anxiety among residents already dealing with uncertainty over health, income and movement. Stakeholders urged officials and community organisations to rely on verified information when communicating with the public.

The economic disruption was expected to continue affecting households even after immediate health restrictions were eased. Stakeholders therefore called for recovery planning that would support businesses, restore supply chains and create opportunities for workers whose livelihoods had been interrupted.

As attention shifted towards implementation, political and community stakeholders in Bauchi called for stronger coordination among authorities, neighbouring communities and economic actors. They said regional cooperation could help ensure that public-health measures were implemented effectively while essential goods and services remained available.

The COVID-19 crisis had demonstrated how closely public health, movement and economic activity were connected. Stakeholders maintained that sustained cooperation would be necessary not only to manage the immediate emergency but also to support households and businesses as Bauchi and neighbouring communities worked towards recovery.

headline: Uyo Promotes Digital Payments as COVID-19 Changes Consumer Habits
summary: Businesses and financial stakeholders in Uyo promoted digital payment options as the COVID-19 outbreak changed how consumers and businesses handled transactions. The shift was seen as a way to reduce dependence on cash while helping businesses maintain services during the disruption.
fullStory:
UYO — Businesses and financial stakeholders in Uyo promoted digital payment options as the COVID-19 outbreak changed how consumers and businesses handled transactions. The increased use of electronic payments reflected growing interest in methods that could allow customers to pay for goods and services without relying entirely on physical cash.

The pandemic was creating new concerns about physical contact in commercial transactions. As businesses adjusted their operations to comply with public-health measures, stakeholders said digital payments could provide a convenient alternative for customers and traders where the necessary infrastructure was available.

Small businesses were among those exploring digital payment options. Traders and service providers increasingly used bank transfers, mobile payment platforms and other electronic methods to receive payments from customers. Stakeholders said the transition could help businesses continue operating when movement and face-to-face interactions were limited.

However, access to digital financial services remained uneven. Some residents lacked smartphones, reliable internet connections or familiarity with electronic payment platforms. Stakeholders said expanding digital payments would therefore require greater public awareness and improved access to affordable financial and telecommunications services.

Financial literacy was also identified as an important part of the transition. Customers needed to understand how to use digital payment platforms safely, while business owners needed to know how to confirm transactions and keep accurate records. Stakeholders encouraged users to protect passwords, personal identification numbers and other sensitive information.

The disruption was also highlighting the importance of reliable telecommunications networks. Digital transactions depended on mobile and internet connectivity, and service interruptions could make electronic payments difficult. Stakeholders called for continued investment in communications infrastructure to support the growing demand for digital services.

Businesses were encouraged to provide customers with clear information about accepted payment methods. Stakeholders said transparent procedures could reduce confusion and help customers become more comfortable with electronic transactions.

The increased use of digital payments could also improve business record keeping. Electronic transaction histories could make it easier for some businesses to monitor sales and manage their finances. Stakeholders said this could provide longer-term benefits for enterprises seeking to strengthen their operations after the pandemic.

The shift was also relevant to financial inclusion. Stakeholders said digital platforms could help connect more people to formal financial services, particularly where traditional banking facilities were not easily accessible. However, they stressed that affordability and accessibility would remain important if digital payments were to reach a wider section of the population.

Consumer protection was another concern. Stakeholders urged financial service providers to maintain effective systems for resolving failed or disputed transactions. Customers were encouraged to retain transaction records and report suspicious activity through official channels.

The pandemic was accelerating changes in consumer behaviour that might continue after restrictions were lifted. Businesses that became accustomed to receiving electronic payments could continue offering them as an additional option alongside cash transactions.

As attention shifted towards implementation, financial and business stakeholders in Uyo called for greater awareness, reliable digital infrastructure and stronger consumer protection. They said these measures would help residents and businesses take advantage of digital payment services while reducing the risks associated with the transition.

The COVID-19 outbreak had created significant disruption for businesses and consumers, but it was also encouraging wider adoption of digital tools. Stakeholders maintained that stronger digital payment systems could support commercial activity during the crisis and contribute to a more efficient local economy in the future.

headline: Asaba Begins Exam Reform Review as COVID-19 Disrupts School Calendar
summary: Education stakeholders in Asaba began reviewing examination arrangements as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted the school calendar and raised concerns about how students would complete their academic programmes. Attention focused on protecting students while developing practical plans for examinations and academic continuity.
fullStory:
ASABA — Education stakeholders in Asaba began reviewing examination arrangements as the COVID-19 outbreak disrupted the school calendar and raised concerns about how students would complete their academic programmes. The closure of schools and restrictions on public gatherings created uncertainty around examinations, assessments and other activities that normally required students and teachers to be physically present.

Stakeholders said the disruption required careful planning to protect students while ensuring that academic standards were maintained. They noted that examination arrangements would need to reflect the public-health situation and any directives issued by relevant authorities.

Students preparing for major examinations were among those facing uncertainty. Many had already completed substantial portions of their programmes before schools were closed, but the interruption affected revision schedules and access to teachers and learning materials.

Teachers and school administrators were also adjusting to the disruption. Some were exploring remote communication with students through messaging platforms and other available tools. Stakeholders said such methods could help students maintain contact with teachers, although access to devices and internet services varied among households.

The situation raised concerns about students from disadvantaged backgrounds. Not all families had reliable internet connections, computers or smartphones that could support online learning. Education stakeholders said any examination or learning plan needed to consider these differences to avoid placing some students at an unfair disadvantage.

Parents were also seeking clearer information about the academic calendar. Many households needed to know when schools could reopen and how examinations would be rescheduled. Stakeholders called for regular communication from education authorities to reduce uncertainty and help families prepare.

The health and safety of students, teachers and examination personnel remained a major consideration. Stakeholders said any eventual return to examination centres would require appropriate sanitation, crowd management and other public-health precautions.

School administrators were encouraged to review examination facilities and identify practical ways of reducing congestion. Where possible, staggered schedules and other arrangements could help limit the number of students gathering at examination centres at the same time.

The disruption also highlighted the importance of contingency planning in the education sector. Stakeholders said schools and education authorities could benefit from developing stronger systems for maintaining learning activities during emergencies, including greater use of digital resources and alternative communication channels.

Education experts cautioned against rushing examination decisions without considering students' readiness. They said students should be given sufficient time to revise and complete required learning activities before assessments were conducted.

Stakeholders also urged authorities to maintain fairness and transparency in any revised examination arrangements. Students and parents needed clear information about dates, procedures and requirements well in advance of examinations.

As attention shifted towards implementation, education stakeholders in Asaba called for coordinated planning among schools, teachers, parents and education authorities. They said the objective should be to protect students while ensuring that examination processes remained credible and accessible.

The COVID-19 outbreak had created an unprecedented disruption to the academic calendar, but stakeholders maintained that careful planning could reduce its long-term effects. They urged education authorities to use the experience to strengthen emergency preparedness and develop more flexible systems for supporting students during future disruptions.

headline: COVID-19 Pandemic Disrupts Economic Activities Across Nigeria
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted economic activities across Nigeria as lockdowns, movement restrictions and declining consumer demand affected businesses and households. Small businesses and informal workers faced significant losses as supply chains weakened and commercial activities slowed.
fullStory:
ABUJA — Nigeria's economy faced significant disruption following the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic, as lockdowns, movement restrictions and declining consumer demand affected businesses across multiple sectors. Commercial activities slowed as companies adjusted their operations to comply with public-health measures introduced to contain the spread of the virus.

Small and medium-sized enterprises were among the businesses most affected by the disruption. Many experienced declining patronage, interruptions to supply chains and difficulties meeting operating costs. Some businesses temporarily suspended operations as restrictions limited movement and reduced customer traffic.

Informal-sector workers also faced serious challenges. Traders, artisans, transport operators and service providers who depended largely on daily earnings reported significant reductions in income. Restrictions on markets, transportation and other commercial activities made it difficult for many workers to maintain their normal livelihoods.

The manufacturing sector was affected by disruptions to the movement of raw materials and finished products. Businesses dependent on imported inputs also faced additional difficulties as international trade and logistics were affected by the wider global crisis. Stakeholders said these challenges placed further pressure on production and employment.

Transportation was similarly disrupted. Restrictions on movement reduced passenger traffic and affected operators whose incomes depended on regular journeys. The hospitality and entertainment sectors faced particularly severe pressure as hotels, restaurants, events and other businesses experienced sharp declines in activity.

Households were also affected as businesses reduced operations and some workers lost income. Reduced earnings made it more difficult for families to meet daily expenses, while uncertainty about the duration of the disruption increased concerns about household financial security.

In response to the economic difficulties, the Federal Government announced various intervention and relief measures intended to support vulnerable households, businesses and workers. Financial institutions also introduced measures aimed at providing temporary relief and improving access to credit for some affected enterprises.

However, stakeholders stressed that the effectiveness of intervention programmes would depend on proper implementation and accessibility. Small businesses and informal workers often faced difficulties accessing formal financial services, making it important for support programmes to reach beneficiaries through practical and transparent channels.

The pandemic also accelerated interest in digital business models. Some companies and traders began relying more heavily on online communication, electronic payments and delivery services as consumers reduced physical visits to shops and commercial centres. Stakeholders said the increased adoption of digital tools could become an important part of the recovery process.

Economists said the crisis exposed structural weaknesses in the Nigerian economy, including heavy dependence on certain sectors and limited social protection for vulnerable workers. They argued that recovery planning should address these weaknesses while encouraging investment in productive sectors and strengthening domestic supply chains.

The disruption also renewed calls for economic diversification. Stakeholders said greater support for agriculture, manufacturing, technology and other productive sectors could reduce the country's vulnerability to future external shocks and create more sustainable employment opportunities.

As economic activities gradually adjusted to the new conditions, businesses and policymakers faced the challenge of balancing public-health measures with the need to restore commercial activity. Stakeholders called for clear policies, continued support for affected enterprises and coordinated efforts to protect jobs and household incomes.

The COVID-19 pandemic created one of the most difficult economic periods experienced by businesses and households in Nigeria in recent years. Stakeholders maintained that effective implementation of relief measures, investment in productive sectors and stronger economic planning would be essential to rebuilding activity and improving the country's resilience against future crises.
