headline: PEARLs Quiz Competition Rewards Nigerian Schools for Academic Excellence
summary: The 2026 NEPL/Seplat Energy PEARLs Quiz Competition concluded with Notre Dame College, Ozoro, winning the overall title. The competition involved 476 secondary schools across Edo and Delta states.
fullStory: BENIN CITY — The 2026 edition of the NEPL/Seplat Energy PEARLs Quiz Competition has concluded with Notre Dame College, Ozoro, Delta State, emerging overall winner. The competition brought together secondary schools from Edo and Delta states and was designed to promote academic excellence, confidence, innovation and character among students. A total of 476 schools participated in the competition before the finalists reached the grand stage. Notre Dame College won the championship trophy and received a N10 million education infrastructure grant. Henson Demonstration School in Benin City finished second and received N5 million, while Lumen Christi College placed third and received N3 million. Students and supervising teachers from the leading schools also received educational support prizes. The competition provides an example of how academic contests can encourage students to develop stronger interest in learning. Quiz competitions require participants to read widely, recall information quickly and work effectively under pressure. They can also expose students to subjects beyond the narrow requirements of classroom examinations. The PEARLs competition has become a platform through which schools can showcase the academic abilities of their students. For participating schools, success can boost confidence among students and teachers while encouraging greater investment in academic activities. The education infrastructure grants attached to the competition also provide direct support to schools. Schools can use such funding to improve learning facilities, purchase educational materials or support other projects that benefit students. Infrastructure remains an important issue in Nigerian education. Many schools require better classrooms, laboratories, libraries, furniture and other facilities. Private-sector support can complement government investment when it is properly coordinated with the needs of schools. The involvement of a major energy company in an education programme also reflects the broader role businesses can play in supporting communities. Corporate social responsibility programmes can contribute to education while creating opportunities for students to interact with organisations outside the school environment. However, long-term education improvement still requires sustained public investment. Competitions and grants can provide valuable support, but they cannot replace the need for adequate government funding, qualified teachers and reliable school infrastructure. The success of the PEARLs competition also highlights the academic potential among young Nigerians. Students across the country regularly demonstrate strong performance in national and international competitions when they receive appropriate preparation and support. Such achievements can challenge perceptions that Nigerian students lack access to quality academic opportunities. Teachers play an important role in preparing students for competitions. Effective preparation requires more than memorising facts. Students need to understand concepts, develop critical-thinking skills and learn how to apply knowledge. Teachers who encourage curiosity can help students develop a lasting interest in learning. Parents and communities can also support students by providing conducive environments for study. Academic achievement is often the result of cooperation among students, teachers, parents and school administrators. The PEARLs competition provides an opportunity to celebrate that collective effort. The participation of hundreds of schools also demonstrates the appetite for academic competitions among secondary-school students. Expanding such opportunities could help identify talented students and encourage them to pursue further education. The winners can serve as role models for other students, showing that hard work and preparation can produce recognition. For Notre Dame College, the N10 million infrastructure grant provides an opportunity to strengthen the school's learning environment. Henson Demonstration School and Lumen Christi College also received substantial support for their achievements. The competition therefore combined recognition with practical educational assistance. The 2026 edition has reinforced the value of academic competitions as part of a broader education strategy. More programmes that encourage reading, science, mathematics, innovation and problem-solving could help Nigerian students develop the skills needed for higher education and employment. The challenge will be ensuring that such opportunities reach students across different regions and socioeconomic backgrounds. For now, the achievements of the participating schools provide a positive example of academic excellence and the potential impact of targeted educational support.

headline: Nigeria's Economy Expected to Continue Gradual Recovery in Second Half of 2026
summary: The Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise projected continued gradual economic recovery in Nigeria during the second half of 2026. It identified financial services, telecommunications, construction, trade and oil refining as potential growth drivers.
fullStory: LAGOS — Nigeria's economy is expected to remain on a gradual recovery path during the second half of 2026, according to an outlook by the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise. The organisation said improvements in financial services, telecommunications, construction, trade and oil refining could support economic activity during the period. The projection comes as Nigeria enters the second half of the year with some signs of improved macroeconomic stability. Exchange-rate conditions have become more stable compared with earlier periods, while inflation has shown signs of moderation and crude-oil production has improved. However, the economic recovery has not yet translated into stronger living standards for many households and businesses. High operating costs continue to affect companies, while consumers remain concerned about food prices and household expenses. The CPPE therefore described the recovery as gradual and fragile. One of the major risks identified by the organisation is the increasing political activity ahead of the 2027 general elections. Election-related spending can increase demand in some sectors, but excessive political uncertainty can also distract policymakers from economic reforms. Businesses and investors require a predictable policy environment to make long-term decisions. Continued implementation of economic reforms will therefore be important. Nigeria has undertaken major policy changes in recent years, including reforms affecting the foreign-exchange market, fuel subsidies and public finances. These measures have generated significant short-term pressure but are intended to improve the structure of the economy. The effectiveness of the reforms will depend partly on whether they produce stronger investment, productivity and employment. Oil remains an important source of government revenue and foreign exchange. Improved production could strengthen public finances and external reserves, but the economy remains vulnerable to changes in global oil prices. Diversifying sources of growth is therefore essential. The financial-services sector is one area that has shown resilience. Banks and other financial institutions support economic activity by providing credit, payment services and investment channels. However, high interest rates can make borrowing difficult for businesses, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises. Telecommunications is another major sector. Nigeria's large digital market continues to support investment in mobile communications, internet services and digital businesses. Expansion of digital infrastructure can improve productivity across other sectors as well. Construction and trade are also expected to contribute to growth, although businesses in these sectors face high input and logistics costs. Manufacturing remains particularly sensitive to electricity costs, foreign exchange and access to imported raw materials. Lower inflation and greater exchange-rate stability could gradually improve business planning if the trend is sustained. Agriculture remains crucial to food security and employment. However, insecurity, flooding and infrastructure problems continue to affect farmers in some areas. Investment in irrigation, storage, transportation and agricultural processing could help reduce losses and increase productivity. The government will also need to maintain attention on food inflation because improvements in headline economic indicators have limited meaning for households if food remains unaffordable. Job creation is another major challenge. Nigeria's rapidly growing population requires the economy to generate large numbers of productive jobs each year. Growth in sectors such as construction, technology, agriculture and manufacturing could help, but businesses need a supportive operating environment. Stable electricity, reliable transportation, access to finance and clear regulations are important for investment. The CPPE's outlook therefore points to an economy with opportunities but significant risks. Policymakers will need to maintain reform momentum while addressing the social costs of adjustment. Social protection programmes can help vulnerable households cope with economic pressures while longer-term reforms take effect. For businesses and investors, the second half of 2026 will provide an important test of whether Nigeria's recent macroeconomic improvements can develop into sustained growth. Political developments will also influence expectations as parties prepare for the 2027 elections. Maintaining policy consistency and economic stability could strengthen investor confidence. For ordinary Nigerians, however, the most important measure of recovery will be whether prices become more manageable, incomes improve and employment opportunities expand. The economic outlook therefore remains cautiously optimistic but dependent on effective policy implementation.
img: A busy Nigerian market reflecting economic activity as businesses navigate the second half of 2026.
source: Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise

headline: Tinubu Directs ICPC to Investigate Controversial Presidential Council Claims
summary: President Bola Tinubu directed the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission to investigate allegations surrounding the purported Presidential Fiscal Policy and Tax Reforms Implementation Council. The investigation followed controversy over the body's status and government budget allocations.
fullStory: ABUJA — President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has directed the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission to investigate allegations surrounding a purported presidential council whose activities and budgetary allocation have generated controversy. The directive came amid competing claims over the status of the Presidential Fiscal Policy and Tax Reforms Implementation Committee and allegations made by Adeniyi Adeyemi, who has been linked to the controversy. The Presidency said the matter required an independent investigation to establish the facts. The dispute has raised questions about the establishment, operation and funding of government bodies and the procedures through which public funds are included in the national budget. The issue became politically sensitive after allegations were made involving government officials. Those named have denied wrongdoing, while the Presidency has rejected claims that the organisation operated as an authorised government body in the manner alleged. President Tinubu's decision to refer the matter to the ICPC places the anti-corruption agency at the centre of efforts to determine what happened. The commission is expected to examine relevant documents and records and establish whether any laws or administrative procedures were violated. The investigation is also expected to clarify the circumstances surrounding budgetary allocations linked to the disputed body. Public budgeting is a central component of government accountability because the national budget determines how public resources are allocated. Government agencies and programmes are expected to have clear mandates and appropriate legal or administrative authority. Questions about the existence or status of an agency receiving public funds therefore require careful investigation. The controversy has generated reactions from politicians, civil society groups and members of the public. Some critics have called for greater transparency and have questioned whether the government has provided sufficient information about the allocation. Government officials have argued that the matter should be resolved through evidence rather than political accusations. The ICPC investigation could help establish the facts. Investigators will need to determine the identities of individuals involved, the documents used to create or represent the organisation and the process through which any budget allocation was made. They may also examine whether funds were released and whether any money was spent. If the investigation finds evidence of fraud or abuse of office, the appropriate legal processes could follow. If the controversy resulted from an administrative error or misunderstanding, the findings could also help clarify responsibility and prevent similar problems. The case comes at a time when public scrutiny of government spending is increasing. Nigerians are demanding stronger accountability as the government implements economic reforms that have increased financial pressure on many households. Transparent use of public funds is therefore important to maintaining public confidence. Anti-corruption agencies have a responsibility to investigate allegations objectively, regardless of the political status of the individuals involved. The credibility of the investigation will depend on the evidence gathered and the transparency of the process. The government has also been under pressure to strengthen its systems for monitoring public spending. Budget preparation involves multiple institutions and large numbers of projects, making effective verification essential. Stronger controls can reduce the risk of unauthorised organisations or questionable projects receiving public funds. The controversy also demonstrates the importance of clear communication from government. When government agencies or committees are created, their mandates and responsibilities should be publicly identifiable. This helps citizens understand which institutions are responsible for particular policies and makes accountability easier. The ICPC has been given a defined period to investigate the matter and report its findings. The outcome is expected to provide clarity on the allegations and determine whether further action is required. For the government, a credible investigation could help resolve the controversy and reinforce its commitment to accountability. For Nigerians, the case offers another test of whether public institutions can investigate politically sensitive allegations without interference. The final findings will therefore be closely watched by political actors, civil society organisations and the wider public.
img: The Presidential Villa in Abuja, where President Bola Tinubu directed an investigation into the controversial council claims.

headline: Lagos Flooding Renews Concerns Over Drainage and Urban Planning
summary: Heavy rainfall caused flooding in several parts of Lagos, renewing concerns over drainage infrastructure, waste disposal and urban planning. Residents in affected areas moved through flooded roads while authorities continued efforts to manage the situation.
fullStory: LAGOS — Heavy rainfall has caused flooding in several parts of Lagos, leaving residents and motorists dealing with waterlogged roads and renewed concerns about the city's drainage infrastructure. Areas including Kunsela Road in Ikate, Shogunle, Oshodi and other communities experienced significant flooding after intense rainfall. Residents in affected areas moved belongings away from floodwater as water levels rose around homes and parked vehicles. The flooding has once again highlighted the difficulty Lagos faces in managing heavy rainfall in a densely populated urban environment. Lagos is a coastal city with extensive low-lying areas, making some communities naturally vulnerable to flooding. Rapid urbanisation has also increased pressure on drainage systems and reduced the amount of open land available for water absorption. Blocked drainage channels can worsen the problem by preventing rainwater from flowing away efficiently. Waste dumped in drainage systems can obstruct the movement of water and increase the likelihood of flooding during heavy rainfall. Authorities have repeatedly urged residents to dispose of waste properly and avoid activities that obstruct waterways. Urban development is another important factor. Construction on wetlands and natural drainage routes can reduce the ability of the environment to absorb or redirect stormwater. Effective planning regulations are therefore necessary to reduce flood risks as the city expands. The Lagos State Government has continued to invest in drainage and flood-control projects, but the scale of the city's infrastructure needs remains significant. Maintenance is also important because even well-designed drainage systems can become ineffective if they are blocked or damaged. Residents have been advised to avoid driving through deep floodwater because vehicles can lose control or become stranded. Pedestrians face risks from open drains and hidden obstacles beneath floodwater. Children are particularly vulnerable and should be kept away from fast-moving or deep water. Flooding can also create public-health risks. Water may become contaminated by sewage, waste and other pollutants. Residents in affected areas need access to clean drinking water and sanitation facilities. Health authorities may need to monitor communities for increases in waterborne diseases after major floods. The economic consequences can also be substantial. Businesses may close temporarily, goods can be damaged and workers may be unable to reach their workplaces. Transport disruptions can increase travel times and raise costs for commuters. Low-income households are particularly vulnerable because they may have limited resources to repair damaged homes or replace lost belongings. Flooding can also affect schools. When roads become impassable, students and teachers may be unable to reach schools. Buildings located in flood-prone areas can also suffer damage. Protecting schools therefore needs to form part of wider flood-management plans. Climate change has increased concerns about extreme rainfall and changing weather patterns. While flooding has multiple causes, intense rainfall can place additional pressure on drainage systems. Cities therefore need stronger adaptation strategies, including improved drainage, flood mapping, early-warning systems and protection of natural waterways. Residents also have a role to play. Keeping drains free of waste, following official warnings and moving valuables to safer locations before severe rainfall can reduce damage. Community-level monitoring can also help authorities identify vulnerable areas. The latest flooding is a reminder that Lagos requires long-term planning rather than only emergency responses after rainfall. Drainage construction, regular maintenance, waste management and enforcement of planning regulations must work together. The immediate priority remains protecting lives and helping affected residents. But the longer-term challenge is building a city capable of coping with heavy rainfall while accommodating continued population growth. As the rainy season progresses, authorities and residents will need to remain vigilant because further heavy rainfall could create additional flooding in vulnerable communities.
img: Floodwater covers a residential road in Lagos after heavy rainfall.
source: Nigeria Hydrological Services Agency; Lagos State Government

headline: Tony Elumelu to Retire as UBA Chairman After Reaching Tenure Limit
summary: United Bank for Africa announced that Tony Elumelu will retire as Group Chairman on August 21, 2026, after completing the maximum tenure allowed for non-executive directors under Central Bank of Nigeria corporate governance rules.
fullStory: LAGOS — United Bank for Africa has announced that Tony Elumelu will retire as Group Chairman of the bank on August 21, 2026, after completing the maximum tenure permitted for non-executive directors under applicable Central Bank of Nigeria corporate governance rules. Elumelu has served as chairman of the financial institution for 12 years. The bank said Emmanuel Nnorom, an existing non-executive director, will succeed him as Group Chairman. The transition marks a significant leadership change for one of Nigeria's largest financial institutions. Elumelu has been a prominent figure in Nigeria's banking and investment sectors and has also become widely known for his activities in entrepreneurship and philanthropy. His tenure at UBA has coincided with the bank's expansion across African markets and the development of its international presence. UBA operates in several African countries as well as financial centres outside the continent. Leadership succession is an important aspect of corporate governance because it allows institutions to maintain continuity while complying with regulatory requirements. The Central Bank of Nigeria has established governance rules governing the tenure of directors in financial institutions. The rules are designed to encourage accountability, reduce excessive concentration of control and promote orderly succession. Elumelu's retirement is therefore part of a regulated transition rather than an indication that he is leaving the financial sector. The appointment of Nnorom provides the bank with an opportunity to maintain institutional continuity. As a non-executive director, he is already familiar with the organisation's governance structure and operations. His experience is expected to help the bank manage the transition while maintaining confidence among customers, employees and investors. UBA's leadership change comes at a time when Nigeria's banking industry is adapting to major changes in the economy. Banks are dealing with evolving regulatory requirements, digital transformation, inflationary pressures and the need to support businesses and households through access to financial services. Technology has become increasingly important in banking as customers use mobile applications and electronic payment systems more frequently. Financial institutions must invest in secure digital infrastructure while protecting customers from fraud and cybercrime. The bank's African operations also expose it to different economic and regulatory environments. Cross-border banking requires effective risk management and strong compliance systems. Leadership continuity can help institutions manage these complexities. Elumelu's departure from the chairmanship does not mark the end of his involvement in business and philanthropy. He remains associated with the Heirs Holdings group and the Tony Elumelu Foundation, which supports African entrepreneurs. His philanthropic initiatives have focused heavily on entrepreneurship and economic empowerment. The transition also highlights the importance of corporate governance in Nigeria's financial sector. Banks manage large amounts of public and private funds and are subject to strict regulatory requirements. Strong boards and transparent leadership succession are essential to maintaining stability. Investors generally monitor leadership changes closely because they can influence corporate strategy and market confidence. UBA will now prepare for the formal transition in August. The bank's board and management will need to ensure that the change occurs smoothly and that strategic priorities remain consistent. Customers are unlikely to experience immediate changes in everyday banking services, but the leadership transition will be watched by investors and industry observers. For Elumelu, completing the maximum permitted tenure represents the end of a long period at the helm of UBA. His time as chairman has been associated with the bank's growth and international expansion. For the institution, the appointment of a successor provides an opportunity to continue that trajectory under new board leadership. The transition demonstrates how regulatory governance rules can shape leadership in major Nigerian financial institutions. As the August handover approaches, attention will turn to the new chairman and the direction the board will take in the next phase of the bank's development.
img: Tony Elumelu at a business event during his tenure as UBA Group Chairman.
source: United Bank for Africa; Central Bank of Nigeria

headline: Ten Killed, Six Injured in Ogun Road Crash on Lagos-Ibadan Expressway
summary: Ten people, including a child, died while six others were injured when a commercial bus collided with a truck at Saapade Bridge on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The Federal Road Safety Corps attributed the crash to speeding, wrongful overtaking and dangerous driving.
fullStory: ABEOKUTA — Ten people were killed and six others injured in a serious road traffic crash at Saapade Bridge along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway in Ogun State. The crash involved a white Sinotruk truck and a white Toyota Hiace commercial bus and occurred at about 8:05 p.m. The Federal Road Safety Corps said 18 people were involved in the accident. The victims included 15 adult males, two adult females and one male child. Ten people, comprising nine adult males and one male child, died in the crash, while six others sustained varying degrees of injuries. Two adult males reportedly escaped without injury. The FRSC attributed the crash to a combination of speeding, wrongful overtaking and dangerous driving. The accident adds to concerns about road safety on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, one of Nigeria's busiest transport corridors. The highway carries large numbers of commercial buses, trucks and private vehicles every day. Heavy traffic, long-distance journeys and the presence of large commercial vehicles can increase the consequences of driving errors. Speeding is particularly dangerous because it reduces the time available for drivers to react to unexpected situations. Wrongful overtaking can also produce head-on collisions or other serious crashes when drivers misjudge the position and speed of other vehicles. Dangerous driving practices remain a major challenge on Nigerian roads. Road safety agencies have repeatedly advised motorists to observe speed limits, maintain safe distances and avoid overtaking in dangerous locations. Commercial transport operators are also expected to ensure that their drivers are properly trained and that vehicles are maintained. Truck drivers have an additional responsibility because heavy vehicles require longer distances to stop. Mechanical faults can also increase the risk of crashes, making regular inspection essential. The Saapade Bridge area is an important section of the highway and carries significant traffic between Lagos and other parts of southwestern Nigeria. Crashes on the route can quickly cause congestion and disrupt movement. Emergency responders therefore have to work rapidly to rescue victims, remove damaged vehicles and restore traffic flow. The human cost of the accident is the most serious concern. Ten deaths in a single crash represent a major loss for families and communities. Road crashes can leave families without breadwinners and create financial pressure through medical expenses and loss of income. Survivors who suffer serious injuries may require prolonged medical treatment and rehabilitation. The incident also highlights the importance of emergency medical response. Rapid access to medical care can make a difference for seriously injured crash victims. Road safety agencies, hospitals, police officers and other responders often need to coordinate at major crash scenes. Preventing such crashes remains preferable to relying only on emergency response. Driver education and enforcement of traffic laws can reduce dangerous behaviour. Authorities can also use road engineering measures, signage and speed controls to improve safety at high-risk locations. Transport companies should monitor drivers and ensure that fatigue does not contribute to dangerous driving. Passengers also have a role by reporting reckless driving and avoiding vehicles that appear unsafe. The FRSC's preliminary findings point to driver behaviour as a major factor in the Ogun crash. Further investigation may establish additional circumstances, but the incident reinforces longstanding warnings about speed and dangerous overtaking. The Lagos-Ibadan Expressway is a vital economic corridor, carrying people and goods between major commercial centres. Keeping the route safe is therefore important not only for individual travellers but also for the wider economy. For the families of those who died, however, the statistics represent individual lives suddenly lost. The accident is another reminder that careful driving and strict compliance with road-safety rules can prevent tragedies. Authorities are expected to continue monitoring the highway and educating motorists, while drivers are urged to exercise greater caution to prevent further loss of life.
img: Emergency responders at the scene of the fatal crash at Saapade Bridge on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

headline: FG Moves to Strengthen Technical Education as Skills Development Takes Centre Stage
summary: The Federal Government intensified efforts to expand technical and vocational education as part of its strategy to equip young Nigerians with practical skills. Officials said stronger skills development would help improve employability and support economic growth.
fullStory: ABUJA — The Federal Government has continued efforts to strengthen technical and vocational education as Nigeria seeks to equip young people with practical skills capable of supporting employment, entrepreneurship and economic development. The renewed attention to technical education comes amid concerns about graduate unemployment and the growing gap between formal academic qualifications and the skills required by employers. Education officials have repeatedly emphasised the importance of giving students access to practical training alongside conventional academic programmes. Technical and vocational education provides students with opportunities to develop skills in areas such as engineering, construction, information technology, agriculture, manufacturing, automobile technology and other trades. Government officials said strengthening these programmes would help young Nigerians become more productive and reduce dependence on limited white-collar employment opportunities. The initiative also forms part of broader efforts to reform Nigeria's education system and make learning more responsive to the needs of the economy. For years, many Nigerian students have focused heavily on university education, while technical colleges and vocational institutions have received less attention. Education experts have argued that this imbalance has contributed to shortages of skilled technicians and artisans in important sectors. Industries often require workers with specialised practical skills, yet employers can struggle to find adequately trained personnel. Expanding technical education could therefore help bridge the gap between education and employment. The government is also expected to improve equipment and training facilities in technical institutions. Modern workshops and laboratories are essential because students need opportunities to work with tools and technologies used in real workplaces. Without adequate equipment, practical courses can become largely theoretical, limiting their usefulness to students. Teacher training is another important component. Instructors must be familiar with modern technologies and industry practices if they are to prepare students effectively. Partnerships between educational institutions and private companies could provide opportunities for instructors and students to gain practical experience. Industry participation can also help institutions update curricula to reflect changing workplace requirements. Digital technology is increasingly becoming part of technical education. Students can now learn skills involving computer programming, digital design, electronics, automation and other technology-based fields. Expanding access to digital training could create additional opportunities for young people, particularly those interested in the growing technology sector. Agriculture is another area where technical education could have a significant impact. Nigeria's agricultural sector requires technicians and skilled workers capable of operating modern equipment, managing irrigation systems, processing agricultural products and maintaining machinery. Training young people in these areas could support productivity and create employment opportunities in rural communities. The government faces challenges in implementing the reforms. Funding remains a major issue across Nigeria's education sector, while many institutions require rehabilitation and modern equipment. Ensuring that programmes are available outside major cities is also important because students in rural communities should not be excluded from opportunities for skills development. Education authorities will therefore need to work closely with state governments and institutions to expand access. The success of technical education will ultimately depend on whether graduates can use their training to secure employment or establish viable businesses. Skills development should be connected to wider economic policies that support small businesses, manufacturing, agriculture and other productive sectors. Access to affordable financing can also help trained young people turn practical skills into businesses. For students and parents, the growing emphasis on technical education represents a broader understanding of what constitutes a successful education. Academic degrees remain important, but practical skills can also provide pathways into employment and entrepreneurship. Nigeria's large youth population makes this particularly important. If young people receive relevant skills and access to opportunities, they can contribute significantly to economic growth. The government's renewed focus on technical and vocational education therefore represents an important part of the wider education reform agenda. Sustained investment, effective management and cooperation with industry will be necessary to turn policy commitments into measurable improvements. If successfully implemented, stronger technical education could help Nigeria develop a more skilled workforce and provide young people with alternatives to traditional academic pathways.

headline: Universities Urged to Expand Research Collaboration and Innovation Programmes
summary: Nigerian universities were urged to strengthen research partnerships with industry and other institutions to improve innovation and national development. Education stakeholders said stronger collaboration could help universities turn research into practical solutions.
fullStory: ABUJA — Nigerian universities have been urged to strengthen research collaboration with government agencies, private companies and international institutions as part of efforts to improve innovation and contribute more directly to national development. Education stakeholders said universities possess significant research capacity but often face challenges in translating academic discoveries into practical products and services. Stronger links between universities and industry could help bridge that gap. Research and innovation are important components of higher education because they allow institutions to contribute to solving problems in areas such as agriculture, healthcare, energy, education, manufacturing and technology. Universities also train researchers and professionals who support the wider economy. However, research activities require adequate funding, laboratories, equipment and access to current academic information. Many Nigerian institutions continue to face constraints in these areas. Stakeholders have therefore called for greater investment in research infrastructure and more competitive funding opportunities for academics and students. Collaboration with private companies could provide another source of support. Businesses can identify practical problems that researchers can help solve, while universities can provide technical expertise and access to specialised facilities. Such partnerships can also give students opportunities to work on real-world projects. Technology has created new opportunities for collaboration. Researchers can work with institutions in other countries through digital platforms, while students can access international journals, databases and academic conferences online. Nigerian universities can benefit from these networks by participating in joint research projects and exchanging knowledge with institutions around the world. Intellectual property protection is also important. Researchers need systems that allow them to protect and commercialise inventions without losing ownership of their work. Universities that establish effective technology-transfer offices can help researchers move promising ideas from laboratories into the marketplace. Entrepreneurship programmes can complement this process by teaching students how to develop business models around innovative products. Research funding remains one of the biggest challenges. Government agencies and university managements must provide reliable funding for projects that address national priorities. Competitive grants can encourage researchers to develop high-quality proposals and demonstrate measurable outcomes. Funding should also extend to postgraduate students because they form an important part of the research workforce. Universities can contribute to national development when research is linked to local needs. Agricultural research, for example, can help farmers improve yields and manage climate-related challenges. Engineering research can support infrastructure development, while computer science and technology research can contribute to digital transformation. Social science research can also help policymakers understand social and economic challenges. The quality of research depends partly on the academic environment. Universities need qualified researchers, modern facilities and sufficient time for academics to conduct studies. Excessive administrative workloads and inadequate resources can limit research productivity. Strengthening postgraduate programmes can also help institutions build a larger pool of researchers. Nigerian universities have produced scholars whose work has attracted international recognition, but stakeholders say more needs to be done to create conditions that allow research to flourish locally. International partnerships can provide access to expertise and equipment, but domestic investment remains essential. The government and university authorities must therefore view research as a long-term investment rather than an occasional expenditure. Students can benefit from stronger research environments as well. Undergraduate and postgraduate students who participate in research projects develop analytical and problem-solving skills that can improve their employment prospects. Innovation programmes can also encourage students to create solutions to local problems. The push for greater research collaboration is therefore about more than academic publications. It is about creating a stronger connection between education, innovation and economic development. If universities, government and industry work together effectively, research findings can have a greater impact on society. For Nigeria, building a knowledge-driven economy will require institutions capable of producing skilled graduates and generating new ideas. Strengthening research collaboration can help universities play that role more effectively.

headline: Flooding Displaces Residents as Heavy Rains Intensify Across Parts of Nigeria
summary: Heavy rainfall caused flooding in several communities as emergency agencies warned residents in vulnerable areas to take precautions. Authorities urged people living near waterways and flood-prone locations to remain alert.
fullStory: ABUJA — Heavy rainfall has increased the risk of flooding in parts of Nigeria, prompting emergency authorities to warn residents in vulnerable communities to take precautions. Several areas have experienced waterlogging and flooding following intense rainfall, with roads, homes and local businesses affected in some communities. The continuing rainy season has renewed concerns about the ability of drainage systems to cope with heavy downpours. Flooding is a recurring problem in many Nigerian cities and rural communities, particularly where drainage infrastructure is inadequate or waterways have been obstructed. Poor waste disposal can also contribute to blocked drainage channels, preventing rainwater from flowing away quickly. Emergency agencies have urged residents to avoid crossing flooded roads or waterways because floodwater can conceal open drains, damaged roads and other hazards. Motorists have also been advised to exercise caution during periods of heavy rainfall because visibility can fall sharply and vehicles can lose control on waterlogged roads. The consequences of flooding can extend beyond temporary disruption. Homes may be damaged, businesses can lose goods and equipment, and families may be forced to leave affected areas. Schools can also be disrupted when classrooms become inaccessible or are used as temporary shelters. Farmers face additional risks because excessive rainfall and flooding can destroy crops and livestock. This can affect food supplies and household incomes, particularly in communities that depend heavily on agriculture. Health risks also increase after flooding. Contaminated water can contribute to the spread of waterborne diseases, while stagnant water can create breeding conditions for mosquitoes. Emergency agencies have therefore encouraged residents to maintain safe water and sanitation practices following floods. Climate change has increased attention on the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events. While individual floods have multiple causes, changing rainfall patterns can increase the risk of unusually heavy precipitation in some regions. Nigerian authorities have been developing flood preparedness and early-warning measures to reduce the impact of disasters. Effective early warnings are particularly important for communities located near rivers and other waterways. Residents who receive timely information can move people and valuables to safer locations before water levels become dangerous. Urban planning is another important factor. Construction on natural waterways and wetlands can restrict the movement of water and increase flood risks. Authorities therefore need to enforce planning regulations and protect natural drainage systems. Investment in drainage infrastructure can also reduce flooding in urban areas. Communities have an important role to play as well. Proper waste disposal helps keep drainage channels clear, while residents can work with local authorities to identify areas where flood protection is needed. Community emergency plans can improve response when flooding occurs. The current rainfall has once again demonstrated the vulnerability of some Nigerian communities to extreme weather. Emergency agencies continue to monitor conditions and advise residents to follow official warnings. Where flooding becomes severe, evacuation may be necessary to protect lives. The priority during any flood emergency is to prevent deaths and ensure that affected people have access to shelter, food, clean water and medical assistance. Longer-term recovery requires rebuilding damaged infrastructure and helping households restore their livelihoods. Preventing future disasters will require a combination of better urban planning, stronger drainage systems, environmental management and reliable early-warning systems. As the rainy season continues, residents in flood-prone areas are being urged to remain vigilant and avoid unnecessary exposure to floodwater.

headline: Political Parties Intensify Preparations Ahead of 2027 General Elections
summary: Political parties across Nigeria intensified preparations for the 2027 general elections as they began organising structures and selecting potential candidates. The Independent National Electoral Commission has continued preparations for the electoral cycle.
fullStory: ABUJA — Political parties across Nigeria have intensified preparations for the 2027 general elections as politicians and party organisations begin positioning themselves for the next electoral contest. The preparations have included consultations among party leaders, mobilisation of supporters and discussions over potential candidates and alliances. The Independent National Electoral Commission has continued preparations for the election in accordance with the established electoral timetable. Political parties are expected to complete a series of administrative and nomination processes before the election. The early preparations reflect the importance of building strong party structures across Nigeria's states and local government areas. Parties seeking national office must mobilise supporters while also maintaining effective internal organisation. Candidate selection is expected to be one of the most important issues facing the parties. Presidential, governorship and legislative aspirants will compete for nominations, potentially creating disagreements within some organisations. Parties will need to manage internal contests carefully to avoid divisions that could affect their performance during the general election. The 2027 election is expected to generate significant political activity because voters will assess the performance of the current administration and consider alternative political platforms. Major issues are likely to include the economy, security, unemployment, education and public infrastructure. The cost of living remains an important concern for many households. Political parties are expected to present policies addressing inflation, employment and economic growth. Security will also remain a major issue as Nigerians continue to demand stronger action against terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other forms of criminal violence. Education is another area likely to feature prominently. Nigeria's large youth population means that access to quality schools, affordable higher education and employment opportunities will be important campaign issues. Parties may also be required to explain how they intend to address the country's out-of-school population and improve technical and vocational training. Electoral credibility will remain another central concern. Political parties and civil society organisations have continued to call for transparent elections, effective voter registration and reliable election technology. INEC has a responsibility to ensure that eligible voters can participate and that electoral processes are conducted according to law. Political parties also have responsibilities, including respecting electoral rules and discouraging violence. Election-related violence has historically affected some parts of Nigeria. Candidates and supporters are expected to avoid inflammatory rhetoric and respect the rights of political opponents. Social media will also play an increasingly important role in the 2027 contest. Political parties can use digital platforms to reach young voters, but misinformation and manipulated content can also influence public debate. Voters will therefore need to evaluate political claims carefully. The growing political activity also creates opportunities for citizens to engage with candidates and demand clear policy proposals. Rather than focusing only on personalities, voters can assess candidates based on their records, programmes and ability to address local and national problems. The coming months are likely to see more political consultations, defections and alliances. Parties will attempt to strengthen their positions before formal campaigns begin. The APC will seek to defend its position at the federal level, while opposition parties will attempt to present competitive alternatives. Smaller parties may also seek to play a greater role through coalitions or regional support. For Nigeria, the success of the 2027 electoral process will depend partly on the ability of political institutions and parties to maintain public confidence. Peaceful elections require cooperation among INEC, security agencies, political parties, candidates, the media and voters. As preparations gather pace, citizens will increasingly be exposed to political messages and campaign activities. The challenge will be to ensure that the political process remains focused on policies and national development rather than division. The 2027 election remains ahead, but the groundwork is already being laid. Political parties that build effective structures, present credible candidates and offer practical solutions will be better positioned to compete when the formal campaign period begins.
