headline: Education Stakeholders Seek Better Funding for Nigerian Schools
summary: Education stakeholders called for stronger and more predictable funding for schools across Nigeria. They said sustained investment was necessary to improve infrastructure, teacher quality, learning materials and access to education.
fullStory: ABUJA — Education stakeholders have renewed calls for increased and more predictable funding for schools across Nigeria, arguing that sustained investment is necessary to improve infrastructure, teaching quality and learning outcomes. The call comes amid continuing concerns about overcrowded classrooms, inadequate facilities, shortages of learning materials and the difficulty many schools face in retaining qualified teachers. Stakeholders said education funding should not be viewed only as an annual budget item but as a long-term investment in the country's human capital. Nigeria has one of Africa's largest and youngest populations, making the quality of its education system particularly important to its future economic development. Basic education remains a major priority because children who receive strong foundational education are better prepared for secondary school, higher education and employment. However, many public schools still require improvements to classrooms, libraries, laboratories, toilets and water facilities. Poor infrastructure can affect attendance and create difficult conditions for both students and teachers. Teacher quality is equally important. Schools require sufficient numbers of qualified teachers who have access to professional development and appropriate teaching resources. Continuous training can help teachers adopt modern teaching methods and respond to changing educational needs. Digital technology is increasingly relevant to education, but access remains uneven. Some schools have reliable internet and computer facilities, while others lack electricity or basic equipment. Expanding digital access could provide students with additional learning resources, but technology investment must be accompanied by teacher training and reliable infrastructure. Education funding also needs to address the needs of vulnerable children. Poverty, insecurity, displacement and disability can create barriers to school attendance. Children from poor households may struggle to afford uniforms, books, transportation and other school-related expenses. In conflict-affected areas, schools may be damaged or closed, while families may relocate and lose access to education. Girls can face additional barriers in some communities. Supporting vulnerable students therefore requires policies that go beyond classroom construction. School feeding programmes, scholarships, safe transportation and inclusive facilities can help reduce barriers to attendance. Technical and vocational education should also receive attention because not every student will follow a traditional university pathway. Skills-based education can prepare young people for employment in construction, agriculture, manufacturing, technology and other sectors. Stronger links between schools and employers could help ensure that training reflects labour-market needs. Funding accountability is another important issue. Increased spending will have limited impact if resources are poorly managed or projects are abandoned. Education authorities must therefore maintain strong monitoring systems and ensure that funds reach schools as intended. Communities can also play a role in monitoring projects and reporting problems. State governments have significant responsibilities because much of basic education administration takes place at the state and local levels. Effective cooperation between federal agencies, state governments and local education authorities can improve the implementation of education programmes. The private sector and development organisations can also contribute, although public authorities remain responsible for ensuring that all children have access to basic education. Stakeholders said Nigeria's education challenges cannot be solved through isolated projects. Long-term planning is needed to ensure that infrastructure, teachers, learning materials, technology and student welfare are addressed together. Education policies should also be based on reliable data so that resources are directed to areas of greatest need. Improving education will require sustained political commitment. Changes in government should not result in the abandonment of effective programmes or major interruptions in funding. Long-term education plans can provide continuity and allow institutions to measure progress. For Nigerian students, the quality of their education will influence their future opportunities. Better-funded schools can provide safer learning environments, stronger teaching and greater access to educational resources. For the country, investment in education can produce a more skilled workforce and support economic growth. The renewed calls for better funding therefore reflect a broader concern about Nigeria's future. If the country is to benefit from its large young population, it will need to provide children and young adults with the education and skills necessary to participate productively in society. Sustained funding, accountability and effective implementation will remain central to that effort.

headline: France Defeat Morocco 2-0 to Reach 2026 World Cup Semi-Finals
summary: France defeated Morocco 2-0 in the 2026 FIFA World Cup quarter-final to secure a place in the semi-finals. The result ended Morocco's historic run and kept France's title defence alive.
fullStory: France defeated Morocco 2-0 in the quarter-final of the 2026 FIFA World Cup to advance to the semi-finals. The match, played on July 9, ended Morocco's impressive campaign and maintained France's hopes of winning another world title. France entered the match as one of the tournament's leading contenders, while Morocco had already made history by reaching the latter stages of the competition. The Moroccan side had attracted widespread attention during the tournament after producing a series of strong performances against established football nations. Their progress had also generated considerable excitement across Africa, where supporters followed the team's campaign as a continental success story. France, however, controlled much of the quarter-final and eventually secured a two-goal victory. The result means France will continue its defence of the World Cup title won at the previous tournament. The French team has developed a reputation for combining experienced international players with a younger generation of talented footballers. Its depth has been particularly important during a tournament in which teams must play several high-pressure matches within a short period. Morocco's elimination nevertheless represents another significant achievement for African football. The North African side had already demonstrated that African teams can compete deep into major international tournaments. Morocco's previous World Cup success had helped change perceptions about the continent's ability to challenge the strongest football nations, and its latest run has reinforced that progress. For Moroccan supporters, the defeat was disappointing, but the team's performance remains a source of pride. The quarter-final also attracted attention in Nigeria because the Super Eagles failed to qualify for the tournament. Nigerian football supporters have watched the competition closely while debating what the country's football authorities need to do to restore Nigeria's place among the world's leading national teams. The success of Morocco has been cited by African football observers as evidence that strong youth development, effective administration and long-term planning can produce competitive national teams. France's victory also set up another major semi-final. The defending champions will face the winner of the Spain-Belgium quarter-final, creating another high-profile contest on the road to the final. The tournament has continued to produce strong performances from both traditional football powers and emerging teams. The 2026 World Cup is being staged across the United States, Canada and Mexico, with an expanded field and a larger number of matches than previous editions. The tournament has therefore provided a broader platform for teams from different regions. France's progress keeps one of Europe's strongest teams in contention for the trophy. The French side will now have to recover quickly and prepare for another demanding semi-final. Morocco, meanwhile, can return home with the knowledge that its campaign has strengthened its reputation on the international stage. The country's performance is likely to influence football development discussions across Africa, particularly around youth academies, coaching and national-team preparation. The quarter-final victory therefore had significance beyond the scoreline. France moved one step closer to another World Cup title, while Morocco continued to demonstrate the growing competitiveness of African football.
img: France players celebrate after defeating Morocco in the 2026 FIFA World Cup quarter-final.

headline: Two Killed in Ogun Road Crash on Sagamu-Benin Expressway
summary: Two people were killed when a Mack truck and a Peugeot J5 bus collided near Ogbere Junction in Ogun State. The Federal Road Safety Corps attributed the crash preliminarily to route and speed violations.
fullStory: ABEOKUTA — Two people were killed in a road traffic crash at Ogbere Junction along the Sagamu-Benin Expressway in Ogun State. The accident occurred at about 5:10 a.m. and involved a white Mack truck and an orange Peugeot J5 bus. According to the Federal Road Safety Corps, four adult males were involved in the crash. Two of the occupants died, while the remaining two escaped without injuries. The impact caused the front section of the Peugeot bus to catch fire and become severely damaged. FRSC officials arrived at the scene and began emergency response procedures, including removing the damaged vehicles and managing traffic around the accident location. Preliminary findings by the road safety agency indicated that route violation and excessive speed were possible causes of the collision. The agency said a fuller investigation would be required before all circumstances surrounding the crash could be established. Road crashes remain a major public safety concern in Nigeria, particularly along heavily travelled interstate highways. The Sagamu-Benin corridor carries significant commercial and passenger traffic and is frequently used by trucks, buses and private vehicles travelling between major cities in the South-West and South-South regions. Speeding, dangerous overtaking, vehicle defects, fatigue and violations of traffic regulations have repeatedly been identified as factors contributing to serious crashes on Nigerian roads. Heavy commercial vehicles can pose additional risks because of their size and stopping distance. The condition of roads and traffic management can also affect safety, particularly at junctions where vehicles enter or leave major highways. The latest accident highlights the importance of responsible driving and compliance with road safety regulations. Drivers are expected to observe speed limits, maintain safe distances and avoid manoeuvres that put other road users at risk. Commercial transport operators also have a responsibility to ensure that drivers are properly trained and vehicles are maintained. Emergency response is another important part of road safety. Quick intervention can save lives when victims suffer serious injuries. Firefighters, medical personnel, police officers and FRSC officials often work together at major crash scenes to rescue victims, control traffic and prevent secondary accidents. The two deaths recorded in Ogun add to the human cost of road crashes in Nigeria. Families can lose breadwinners and communities can experience long-term consequences when people are killed or permanently injured in preventable accidents. Beyond the immediate human loss, road crashes also cause economic costs through medical treatment, property damage, lost working time and traffic disruption. Authorities have repeatedly encouraged motorists to exercise caution, particularly during periods of heavy traffic. Drivers using the Sagamu-Benin Expressway are expected to remain alert and comply with speed regulations as they travel through busy junctions and populated areas. The FRSC has also continued public education campaigns aimed at reducing dangerous driving practices. The investigation into the Ogun crash is expected to establish the precise circumstances that led to the collision. If route violation and speeding are confirmed, the findings could reinforce the need for stronger enforcement on the highway. For the families of those who died, however, the investigation cannot undo the loss. The incident is another reminder that road safety depends on the combined responsibility of drivers, transport companies, regulators and other road users. Greater compliance with traffic rules and improved enforcement remain essential to reducing preventable deaths on Nigerian roads.
img: Emergency responders at the scene of a fatal road crash along the Sagamu-Benin Expressway in Ogun State.

headline: Reps Demand Stronger Measures Against South Africa Over Xenophobic Attacks
summary: The House of Representatives called for stronger diplomatic measures against South Africa over renewed xenophobic attacks and threats against Nigerians. The demand came as hundreds of Nigerians returned home through a government-supported evacuation programme.
fullStory: ABUJA — The House of Representatives has called on the Federal Government to take stronger diplomatic measures against South Africa over renewed xenophobic attacks, killings and alleged persecution of Nigerians and other African nationals living in the country. The resolution followed a motion of urgent public importance considered by lawmakers as Nigerian authorities continued an evacuation programme for citizens who wished to leave South Africa because of security concerns. The parliamentary action came as 282 Nigerians arrived at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos on an Air Peace evacuation flight from South Africa. The returnees included children and other vulnerable persons seeking to leave the country amid growing concerns over anti-foreigner sentiment. The evacuation programme was launched after renewed xenophobic tensions in South Africa. Nigerian officials have been engaging South African authorities while assisting citizens who want to return home. The latest flight was the fourth major evacuation operation carried out under the programme. The Federal Government has said the exercise is intended to provide safe passage for Nigerians who feel threatened or who have chosen to leave the country. Xenophobia has periodically strained relations between Nigeria and South Africa. Nigerians living in South Africa have previously reported attacks, intimidation and discrimination, particularly during periods of heightened anti-immigrant sentiment. South African authorities have also faced pressure to protect foreign nationals and prosecute perpetrators of violence. The latest tensions have generated strong reactions in Nigeria, where citizens and political leaders have demanded greater protection for Nigerians abroad. Lawmakers argued that diplomatic pressure was necessary to ensure that the South African government takes stronger action against those responsible for attacks. At the same time, Nigerian officials have warned against retaliatory violence against South African citizens or businesses in Nigeria. Nigeria and South Africa maintain significant economic and diplomatic relations. South African companies operate extensively in Nigeria, while Nigerian businesses and citizens have established commercial and professional links in South Africa. Any escalation of the dispute could therefore have economic consequences for both countries. The government faces the difficult task of protecting Nigerian citizens while maintaining diplomatic relations with South Africa. Evacuation provides immediate assistance to citizens who want to return, but it does not address the deeper causes of xenophobia. Long-term improvement will require stronger law enforcement, diplomatic engagement and efforts to counter misinformation and hostility toward foreign nationals. Economic conditions in South Africa have also contributed to anti-migrant sentiment. High unemployment and concerns over crime have sometimes been blamed on foreigners, although economic research has challenged simplistic claims that migrants are responsible for unemployment among South Africans. Migrants also contribute to sectors of the economy where labour is required. Nigerian organisations in South Africa have continued to call for protection and justice for victims. Some returnees have described frightening experiences and said they no longer felt safe remaining in the country. The Nigerian government has encouraged citizens who want to return to register through the appropriate channels so that evacuation arrangements can be coordinated. The latest evacuation is therefore both a humanitarian operation and a reflection of the seriousness of the diplomatic dispute. Nigeria and South Africa will need to maintain dialogue to prevent the situation from deteriorating further. Protecting citizens remains a central responsibility of both governments. For Nigeria, the immediate priority is ensuring the safe return of citizens who have requested evacuation. For South Africa, addressing xenophobic violence and ensuring equal protection under the law will be essential to restoring confidence among foreign nationals. The House of Representatives' call for stronger action signals growing domestic pressure on the Nigerian government. How the government balances diplomatic relations with the demand for stronger protection of Nigerians abroad will remain an important issue in the weeks ahead.
img: Nigerian returnees arrive in Lagos after being evacuated from South Africa amid xenophobic attacks.
source: House of Representatives; Federal Ministry of Foreign Affairs

headline: Reps Open Probe Into N1.3bn Allocation for Alleged Fake Government Agency
summary: The House of Representatives ordered an investigation into how more than N1.3 billion was allocated in the 2026 budget to the purported Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council. The Presidency has disowned the body and President Tinubu ordered the ICPC to investigate the matter.
fullStory: ABUJA — The House of Representatives has opened an investigation into the inclusion of more than N1.3 billion in the 2026 budget for the purported Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council, an organisation the Presidency has described as non-existent and unauthorised. Lawmakers constituted an ad hoc committee to determine how the body entered the federal budget and whether government processes were compromised. The investigation followed concerns raised in the National Assembly over the legal status of the organisation and the circumstances surrounding its reported activities. Records presented to lawmakers indicated that the purported council had no known Act of the National Assembly establishing it as a federal government agency. Despite this, the organisation was reportedly allocated funds in the 2026 Appropriation framework. The controversy intensified after Adeniyi Adeyemi, who described himself as the council's Director-General, made allegations involving senior government officials. The Presidency rejected the claims and said the organisation was fictitious. President Bola Tinubu subsequently directed the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission to investigate the matter and submit its findings within 30 days. The House's decision to conduct its own investigation reflects concerns about parliamentary oversight and the integrity of the federal budgeting process. Lawmakers said the committee would examine how the organisation was presented within government structures, how funds were allocated to it and whether officials or institutions failed to carry out adequate checks. The controversy has raised wider questions about the systems used to prepare and approve Nigeria's annual budget. Federal budgets contain thousands of individual projects and allocations, making verification and oversight important at every stage. An unauthorised organisation receiving a substantial allocation would raise questions about the effectiveness of those controls. Public finance experts have also stressed the need for transparent documentation and clear legal authority for government agencies. Agencies established by government should have identifiable mandates, legal backing and appropriate accountability mechanisms. The allegations involving the purported council have also become politically sensitive. Opposition figures have called for an independent investigation, arguing that the government should not investigate allegations involving its own officials without broader participation. Government supporters have maintained that the ICPC is legally empowered to investigate corruption-related allegations and should be allowed to complete its work. FCT Minister Nyesom Wike defended President Tinubu's Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, against allegations linking him to the controversy. Wike described the allegations as politically motivated and argued that the investigation should be allowed to establish the facts. Gbajabiamila has denied involvement with the purported organisation. The House committee is expected to examine documents, government records and testimony from relevant officials and individuals. Its findings could help determine whether the budget allocation resulted from administrative error, deliberate manipulation or another process failure. The investigation is important because the federal budget represents public funds and must be subject to accountability. Nigerians have a direct interest in knowing how public resources are allocated and whether institutions receiving money have legal authority to do so. The controversy also demonstrates the importance of effective oversight by both the legislature and anti-corruption agencies. A credible investigation will require evidence rather than political claims. Authorities will need to establish what happened, who was responsible and whether public funds were actually released or spent. If wrongdoing is established, those responsible could face legal and administrative consequences. If the allocation resulted from an error, government systems may need to be strengthened to prevent similar incidents. The House investigation and the ICPC probe are therefore expected to provide important answers. The outcome could influence public confidence in Nigeria's budgetary and governance systems. For now, lawmakers and investigators are expected to establish the facts surrounding the purported agency and the controversial budget allocation.
img: The National Assembly complex in Abuja where lawmakers opened an investigation into the controversial budget allocation.
source: House of Representatives; Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission

headline: UBEC Unlocks More Than N100bn in Basic Education Grants for States and FCT
summary: The Universal Basic Education Commission said it had facilitated access to more than N100 billion in previously unaccessed matching grants for states and the Federal Capital Territory. The funds are being directed towards school infrastructure, teacher development and improved learning outcomes.
fullStory: ABUJA — The Universal Basic Education Commission has facilitated the mobilisation of more than N100 billion in previously unaccessed matching grants for states and the Federal Capital Territory, according to the commission's Executive Secretary, Aisha Garba. The development is part of reforms aimed at improving basic education infrastructure, teacher quality and learning outcomes across Nigeria. Garba disclosed the development during a media engagement with education correspondents in Abuja. She said the funds had remained unaccessed for years because some states faced difficulties meeting the requirements for accessing matching grants. Reforms introduced by UBEC have helped states overcome some of those barriers and gain access to resources intended for basic education development. The commission said the funds are being channelled into projects designed to improve learning environments and expand access to quality education. UBEC works with State Universal Basic Education Boards to finance projects in public primary and junior secondary schools. According to the commission, the interventions have included the construction and renovation of classrooms, provision of toilets and water facilities, and the supply of school furniture. More than 4,600 classrooms have reportedly been constructed and over 6,100 renovated through recent interventions, while hundreds of boreholes and thousands of sanitation facilities have also been provided. The scale of the investment is significant because Nigeria continues to face major challenges in basic education. Many schools, particularly in rural and underserved communities, require better classrooms, furniture, water, sanitation and learning materials. Poor infrastructure can affect both attendance and learning outcomes. Teachers also require continuous professional development to improve their ability to deliver lessons effectively. UBEC said teacher development was another area receiving attention under its strategic reforms. Improving the quality of teaching is important because infrastructure alone cannot guarantee better educational outcomes. Schools need qualified teachers, adequate learning materials and supportive environments. Access to funding has also been a long-standing issue in Nigeria's education sector. Matching grants require states to provide counterpart contributions before federal funds can be accessed. Some states have struggled to meet the requirements, resulting in billions of naira remaining unused for extended periods. UBEC's reforms are intended to make the system more accessible while maintaining accountability. The commission has emphasised the importance of ensuring that funds are used for their intended purposes. State education authorities and SUBEBs are expected to implement projects and provide the necessary oversight. Effective monitoring will be important to prevent delays, abandoned projects or misuse of funds. The mobilisation of the previously inaccessible grants comes at a time when Nigeria is seeking to improve education outcomes and reduce the number of children without access to quality schooling. The country has one of the world's largest populations of out-of-school children, making basic education investment a national priority. Better school infrastructure can also support efforts to keep children in school. Safe classrooms, toilets, clean water and adequate furniture can make schools more attractive to families and reduce barriers to attendance. The funds can also support communities affected by insecurity, displacement and poverty. Schools in vulnerable areas often face additional challenges, including damaged infrastructure and shortages of teachers. Government intervention can help rebuild educational services in such communities. UBEC's announcement therefore represents an important development for basic education financing. The effectiveness of the programme will ultimately depend on how quickly and transparently the funds are converted into useful projects. Parents, teachers and communities will be watching to see whether the increased access to funding produces visible improvements in schools. For Nigeria's education system, unlocking dormant resources is only one part of the challenge. Sustained funding, effective management, teacher development and strong accountability will remain necessary to produce lasting improvements in the quality and accessibility of basic education.

headline: Tinubu Retains Shettima as APC Running Mate for 2027 Presidential Election
summary: President Bola Tinubu has retained Vice-President Kashim Shettima as his running mate for the 2027 presidential election. The APC formally submitted the Tinubu-Shettima ticket as political parties moved to meet the electoral timetable.
fullStory: ABUJA — President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has retained Vice-President Kashim Shettima as his running mate for the 2027 presidential election, ending months of speculation over whether the ruling All Progressives Congress would replace the Vice-President on its ticket. The APC formally submitted the nomination documents of Tinubu and Shettima to the party's National Working Committee in Abuja for onward transmission to the Independent National Electoral Commission. The decision means the ruling party will seek to return the same presidential ticket that contested the 2023 election. Shettima's retention had been the subject of political speculation for several months as politicians and interest groups debated the composition of the APC ticket for the next election. Some groups had called for a change in the ticket, while supporters of the Vice-President argued that his continued partnership with Tinubu provided political continuity. The APC's decision came as political parties faced deadlines for submitting presidential and National Assembly candidates to INEC. The electoral timetable has increased activity within parties as they select candidates and complete the administrative requirements for the 2027 general elections. The Tinubu-Shettima ticket won the 2023 presidential election and has remained at the centre of the APC's governing structure. Their decision to contest again gives the ruling party an opportunity to campaign on the record of the administration while also defending its position against opposition parties. The 2027 election is expected to be highly competitive, with several political parties preparing their own candidates and coalitions. The APC has argued that the administration's economic and infrastructure reforms will form part of its campaign message. The government has introduced significant economic reforms since taking office, including changes to fuel subsidy policy and the foreign exchange system. Supporters say the measures are intended to create a more stable foundation for long-term economic growth, while critics point to the immediate cost-of-living pressures experienced by many households. The political debate is therefore likely to focus heavily on the economy, security, employment and social welfare. Security remains another major issue. Nigerians continue to demand stronger action against terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other forms of criminal violence. The performance of the government in addressing insecurity is expected to influence voter decisions in 2027. The ruling party will also face questions about governance and the delivery of public services. For the opposition, the election provides an opportunity to challenge the APC's record and present alternative policies. The emergence of candidates and alliances in the months ahead will determine the shape of the contest. The retention of Shettima also means the APC will again present a Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket. The same-faith ticket was controversial during the 2023 election and is likely to remain part of political debate during the next campaign. Supporters have defended the arrangement on the basis of competence and political considerations, while critics have continued to argue that Nigeria's religious diversity should be reflected in the composition of the presidential ticket. With the nomination formally settled, attention will now shift to campaign preparations and the wider competition among political parties. The APC will seek to mobilise its governors, lawmakers and party structures across the country, while opposition parties will work to consolidate their own support bases. The 2027 election remains more than a year away, but the formal nomination process marks an important early stage in the political contest. The Tinubu-Shettima ticket will now have to defend its record before Nigerian voters while opposition parties seek to persuade the electorate that they can provide a different direction for the country.

headline: Army Says More Than 300 Bandits Killed in Zamfara Operation
summary: The Zamfara State Government said more than 300 suspected terrorists and bandits were killed during a military operation in Gummi Local Government Area. The operation was described as a major blow against armed groups operating in the state's rural communities.
fullStory: GUSAU — The Zamfara State Government has confirmed that more than 300 suspected terrorists and bandits were killed during a military operation in Gummi Local Government Area. The operation, conducted by Nigerian troops, targeted armed groups operating from camps around the Gummi area. The state government described the operation as a significant development in the fight against banditry and violent crime in the North-West. According to the state authorities, the military offensive was part of continuing operations aimed at dismantling criminal networks that have terrorised communities across Zamfara. The region has faced years of attacks involving bandit groups accused of kidnapping residents, stealing livestock, attacking farmers and imposing illegal levies on rural communities. The latest military operation involved troops supported by local vigilantes, according to accounts from the area. Residents reported intense fighting as security forces confronted armed groups attempting to move from their camps. The scale of the reported casualties could not be independently verified, and the figures were provided by state authorities. Military operations against armed groups have intensified in several North-Western states as security agencies attempt to prevent criminal networks from expanding into new territories. Intelligence gathering and cooperation with local communities have become increasingly important because many armed groups operate in remote forest areas that are difficult for conventional security forces to monitor continuously. Zamfara has been among the states most affected by banditry. Communities in rural areas have suffered repeated attacks, leading to deaths, kidnappings and displacement. Farming activities have also been disrupted as residents fear travelling to their fields. The security situation has therefore had an economic impact in addition to its humanitarian consequences. Agriculture is a major source of livelihood in Zamfara, and insecurity can reduce food production when farmers abandon farmland or are unable to reach their farms safely. The state government has continued to call for cooperation between communities and security agencies. Local intelligence can help troops identify the locations and movements of armed groups, although residents who provide information may face retaliation if their identities are exposed. Security agencies must therefore protect sources and maintain public confidence. The operation also highlights the importance of preventing armed groups from relocating after military pressure. Security analysts have warned that sustained military operations in one area can sometimes push criminal groups toward neighbouring communities. Coordination across state boundaries is therefore necessary to prevent displacement of violence rather than its elimination. Beyond military action, long-term security will require measures that address the conditions that allow criminal groups to recruit and operate. Economic opportunities, education, justice and effective local governance can all contribute to reducing vulnerability to criminal recruitment. The government has also been under pressure to protect farmers and restore access to agricultural land. Safe farming communities would help support food production and reduce the economic effects of insecurity. The reported operation represents a major security development in Zamfara, but officials will still need to determine whether armed groups have been significantly weakened and whether communities can remain safe after troops leave the area. Continued intelligence-led operations and cooperation with local communities will be important. For residents who have lived under the threat of bandit attacks for years, the ultimate measure of success will be whether they can return to their farms, markets and homes without fear. The state government has praised the military and other security personnel involved in the operation and urged them to sustain efforts against armed groups. The authorities are expected to continue monitoring the affected areas and conducting further operations where necessary.
