source: Recording Industry Association of Nigeria; IFPI

headline: South Africa's Government Moves to Tighten Response to Xenophobic Violence
summary: South African authorities faced renewed pressure to protect foreign nationals and address violence linked to anti-immigrant sentiment. The developments have also raised concerns in Nigeria, where officials continue to monitor the safety of Nigerians living and doing business in South Africa.
fullStory: PRETORIA — South African authorities are facing renewed pressure to strengthen the protection of foreign nationals and respond more effectively to xenophobic violence as concerns over attacks against migrants continue to affect communities and relations with other African countries. The issue has particular significance for Nigeria because thousands of Nigerians live, work and operate businesses in South Africa. Previous waves of anti-immigrant violence have repeatedly strained relations between Abuja and Pretoria, prompting calls for stronger law enforcement and greater protection for foreign nationals. South African authorities have maintained that criminal acts against migrants should be handled through the country's justice system and have condemned violence directed at people because of their nationality. However, migrant communities and advocacy groups have continued to call for more effective preventive measures. Xenophobic violence in South Africa has often been linked to economic frustrations, including unemployment, competition for jobs and perceptions that foreign nationals are responsible for crime or pressure on public services. Researchers and rights organisations have repeatedly challenged such claims, arguing that migrants are frequently scapegoated for broader social and economic problems. Nigeria has consistently urged South Africa to protect Nigerian citizens and ensure that perpetrators of attacks are held accountable. The two countries maintain extensive political and economic relations, and both are influential members of the African Union. South African companies operate in Nigeria while Nigerian businesses and professionals have established significant economic interests in South Africa. The relationship therefore extends well beyond migration issues. Diplomatic tensions can nevertheless emerge quickly when Nigerians are killed, injured or have their businesses attacked. Nigerian officials have in previous cases summoned South African diplomats and demanded explanations when serious incidents occur. Pretoria has similarly engaged Abuja when concerns have arisen over the treatment of South African citizens or businesses in Nigeria. Maintaining communication between the two governments is therefore important for preventing individual incidents from developing into wider diplomatic disputes. South African police and other authorities have the responsibility of protecting people within the country regardless of nationality. Effective policing can help prevent attacks and ensure that those responsible for violence face prosecution. Authorities also need to address misinformation and inflammatory rhetoric that can contribute to hostility toward migrants. Community organisations have called for greater public education and stronger engagement between migrants and local residents. Economic conditions remain a major part of the discussion. South Africa continues to face high unemployment, particularly among young people. Competition for employment can create resentment toward migrant workers, even when the underlying causes of unemployment are more complex. Migrants also contribute to the economy through employment, entrepreneurship, taxes and consumer spending. Nigerian entrepreneurs in South Africa operate businesses in sectors including retail, technology, entertainment and professional services. Their economic contributions are often overshadowed when public debate focuses exclusively on migration-related problems. The issue also has a regional dimension. Free movement and migration are common across Africa, where people frequently move between countries in search of employment, education and business opportunities. Attacks against migrants can therefore have consequences beyond the country where they occur. Governments across the continent have an interest in ensuring that citizens living abroad are treated fairly and that disputes are resolved through legal and diplomatic channels. Nigeria has historically played an important role in supporting anti-apartheid struggles and promoting African solidarity. Its relationship with South Africa has therefore carried considerable political significance since the end of apartheid. Both countries have continued to cooperate on continental issues despite occasional disagreements. Protecting their citizens and businesses is an important part of maintaining that relationship. For South Africa, the challenge is to ensure that legitimate concerns about crime and economic hardship do not become justification for collective punishment of migrants. Law enforcement must distinguish between individual criminal behaviour and nationality. For Nigeria, the priority remains ensuring that its citizens receive adequate protection while maintaining constructive diplomatic engagement with Pretoria. Stronger cooperation between the two countries could help establish better mechanisms for responding quickly to incidents involving migrants. Such mechanisms could include improved consular communication, faster reporting of attacks and closer cooperation between police authorities. The continuing debate over xenophobia highlights broader questions about migration, unemployment and social cohesion in South Africa. Addressing those problems will require more than security operations alone. Economic opportunities, accurate public information and effective institutions will also be necessary. For Nigerians living in South Africa, however, the immediate concern remains safety and the ability to work and conduct business without fear of attack. The Nigerian and South African governments will therefore face continued pressure to turn their diplomatic commitments into practical protection for citizens and communities.
img: South African police officers monitoring a public area amid continuing concerns over xenophobic violence and attacks on foreign nationals.

headline: Trump Praises Tinubu's Security Efforts as Nigeria and US Deepen Counterterrorism Cooperation
summary: U.S. President Donald Trump praised President Bola Tinubu's efforts to address violence in Nigeria and reaffirmed Washington's support for the country in combating terrorism. The development comes as Nigeria and the United States continue efforts to strengthen security cooperation and intelligence sharing.
fullStory: ABUJA — U.S. President Donald Trump has praised President Bola Tinubu's leadership and efforts to address violence in Nigeria, signalling an improvement in relations between Abuja and Washington after tensions over Nigeria's handling of insecurity. In a letter dated July 6 and released by the Nigerian presidency on July 22, Trump expressed appreciation for Tinubu's actions and reaffirmed U.S. support for Nigeria's efforts to combat terrorism. Trump said he appreciated what he described as Tinubu's decisive leadership on behalf of the Nigerian people and pledged U.S. support in efforts to make Nigeria stronger and more prosperous. The message marked a notable change in tone compared with the previous year, when Trump had publicly criticised Nigeria over the security of Christian communities and threatened possible measures against the country. Nigerian authorities rejected those accusations, maintaining that insecurity affects citizens across religious and ethnic lines. The latest message reflects a broader effort by the two countries to strengthen their security relationship. Nigeria and the United States have established a joint security working group intended to expand intelligence sharing, training and cooperation against militant groups. The framework is designed to improve the ability of both countries to identify security threats and coordinate responses. Nigeria continues to face several forms of insecurity. Armed groups have carried out attacks and kidnappings in parts of the North-West, while insurgency remains a serious concern in the North-East. Other regions have also experienced communal violence, criminal activity and attacks on communities. The scale and nature of the threats have made international security cooperation an important part of Nigeria's counterterrorism strategy. The United States has provided Nigeria with security assistance, training and intelligence support over the years. American cooperation has included efforts to strengthen the capabilities of Nigerian security agencies and improve their ability to respond to extremist organisations. The relationship has nevertheless been affected by disagreements over human rights, religious violence and the conduct of security operations. Trump's latest message suggests that both governments are seeking to place greater emphasis on cooperation. The release of the letter also came shortly after U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for Africa Frank Garcia visited Abuja for discussions with Nigerian officials. The visit provided an opportunity for both sides to examine security cooperation and other areas of bilateral relations. For Nigeria, stronger cooperation with Washington could provide access to additional intelligence, training and technical support. Intelligence sharing can be particularly valuable in tracking militant networks and identifying threats before attacks occur. Nigerian security agencies still have primary responsibility for operations within the country, but international partners can provide information and technical capabilities that complement domestic efforts. The security relationship also has wider diplomatic implications. Nigeria is one of Africa's most populous countries and an important political and economic power in West Africa. Strong relations between Abuja and Washington can influence cooperation on regional security, trade, development and other international issues. Nigeria also plays an important role in regional efforts to combat terrorism and organised crime. The government has welcomed international support while insisting that Nigeria must retain responsibility for determining how security operations are conducted within its territory. The challenge for Nigerian authorities remains translating diplomatic support into measurable improvements in security. Communities affected by attacks and kidnappings continue to demand better protection, faster responses and stronger action against criminal networks. Public confidence in security institutions will depend largely on whether those improvements are visible on the ground. The latest exchange between Nigeria and the United States therefore represents more than a diplomatic gesture. It demonstrates an effort to rebuild trust and strengthen practical cooperation after a period of public disagreement. Both governments now have an opportunity to deepen intelligence sharing, improve training and coordinate efforts against extremist and criminal groups. For Nigeria, the ultimate test will be whether stronger international cooperation contributes to fewer attacks and greater safety for communities. For the United States, closer cooperation with Abuja provides an opportunity to support security and stability in one of Africa's most strategically important countries.
img: President Bola Tinubu of Nigeria during a diplomatic engagement as Nigeria and the United States strengthen security cooperation.

headline: Nigeria Moves to Expand Digital Learning as Schools Seek Better Access to Technology
summary: Education authorities continued efforts to expand digital learning and improve access to technology in Nigerian schools. The initiative is aimed at helping students and teachers benefit from digital resources while addressing gaps in educational access.
fullStory: ABUJA — Nigeria's education authorities are continuing efforts to expand digital learning and improve access to technology in schools as the country seeks to modernise teaching and provide students with wider access to educational resources. Digital education has become increasingly important as schools and universities adopt online resources, electronic learning platforms and other technology-based tools. The push is also intended to address disparities in access to learning materials between urban and rural communities. Education technology can give students access to textbooks, recorded lessons, academic databases and other resources that may not be available in their immediate communities. For teachers, digital tools can provide additional materials for lesson preparation and professional development. However, the effectiveness of digital learning depends heavily on access to electricity, internet connectivity, affordable devices and trained teachers. These remain significant challenges in many parts of Nigeria. Rural schools in particular can struggle with unreliable electricity and limited telecommunications coverage, making it difficult to use online learning platforms consistently. The government has therefore faced pressure to improve basic infrastructure alongside the introduction of digital education programmes. Expanding broadband access is an important part of the process. Students cannot benefit fully from online resources when internet connections are unreliable or too expensive for families to afford. Public investment and partnerships with telecommunications companies can help improve connectivity, particularly in underserved communities. Schools also need appropriate equipment. Computers, tablets, projectors and other devices can support digital instruction, but maintaining those devices requires funding and technical support. Schools that receive equipment without adequate maintenance arrangements may find that the technology becomes unusable after a relatively short period. Teacher training is another important consideration. Technology cannot automatically improve education if teachers are not comfortable using digital tools in the classroom. Training programmes can help teachers integrate online resources into lessons and use technology to assess student performance. Digital literacy can also help students develop skills that will be useful in higher education and the workplace. Nigeria's large youth population makes these skills increasingly important. Employers across many sectors are seeking workers who can use digital tools, analyse information and communicate effectively through technology. Improving digital education can therefore contribute to both academic outcomes and future employability. The government has also explored ways to use digital platforms to support students who cannot attend traditional classrooms. This can be particularly useful during emergencies that disrupt schooling, including insecurity, natural disasters or public-health crises. Online and broadcast learning systems can provide continuity when physical schools are temporarily unavailable. However, digital education cannot replace the need for safe and adequately staffed physical schools. Many students benefit from direct interaction with teachers and classmates, while younger children in particular may require supervision that online learning cannot easily provide. Digital tools are therefore most effective when they complement rather than completely replace classroom teaching. Affordability remains another challenge. Families with limited incomes may struggle to purchase smartphones, computers or data subscriptions. If digital learning expands without addressing this gap, existing inequalities could become wider because wealthier students would have greater access to educational technology. Government programmes therefore need to consider how devices and connectivity can be made available to disadvantaged students. The expansion of digital learning also raises questions about online safety and responsible use of technology. Students need guidance on protecting personal information, identifying unreliable information and avoiding harmful online content. Teachers and parents have important roles to play in developing those skills. Education authorities must also ensure that digital platforms used by schools meet appropriate privacy and security standards. Despite the challenges, technology offers significant opportunities for Nigeria's education system. Digital resources can expand access to knowledge, support teachers and allow students to learn beyond the limits of traditional textbooks. The benefits are likely to be greatest when technology investment is combined with improvements in electricity, internet access, teacher training and school infrastructure. Nigeria's continued investment in digital learning therefore represents part of a broader effort to modernise education and prepare students for an increasingly technology-driven economy. The success of the strategy will depend not simply on providing devices but on ensuring that schools have the infrastructure, teachers and support systems required to use them effectively.

headline: Nigeria's Oil Output Rises as Government Intensifies Efforts to Curb Crude Theft
summary: Nigeria continued efforts to raise crude oil production as authorities stepped up measures against oil theft and attacks on petroleum infrastructure. Higher production is important to government revenue and foreign-exchange earnings as the country works to strengthen its economy.
fullStory: ABUJA — Nigeria is intensifying efforts to increase crude oil production and reduce losses from oil theft as the government seeks to strengthen revenue and foreign-exchange earnings from the petroleum sector. Crude oil remains one of the country's most important sources of government income and foreign currency, making production levels a major factor in Nigeria's economic outlook. For years, oil theft and vandalism have reduced the amount of crude reaching export terminals. Criminal networks have tapped pipelines and other infrastructure, while damaged facilities have forced operators to shut down production or carry out expensive repairs. The resulting losses have affected government revenue and reduced the country's ability to take full advantage of periods of strong international oil prices. The government and petroleum industry have therefore increased surveillance and security operations around producing areas and pipelines. Security agencies have worked with oil companies and local communities to identify illegal connections and disrupt the networks involved in crude theft. Authorities have also sought greater cooperation from communities in oil-producing areas, where local information can help identify suspicious activity and protect infrastructure. Increasing production is important because Nigeria's public finances remain closely linked to oil revenues. Although successive governments have promoted economic diversification, crude oil continues to account for a substantial share of export earnings. Higher production can therefore improve the supply of foreign currency and provide additional revenue for government programmes. The country's foreign-exchange market has faced significant pressure in recent years, with the naira undergoing major adjustments after reforms introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria. Increased oil earnings could help strengthen the external position and provide additional liquidity to the economy. The petroleum sector is also important for attracting investment. International and domestic oil companies require confidence that production facilities can operate safely and that commercial conditions are sufficiently stable to justify long-term investment. Persistent theft and vandalism increase operating costs and can discourage investment in new projects. Improving security can therefore support both current production and future development. Nigeria has also been working to improve the regulatory environment for the petroleum industry following the implementation of the Petroleum Industry Act. The legislation was intended to create a clearer framework for investment, improve governance and strengthen the commercial performance of the national oil company and other industry participants. The government has sought to use the reforms to attract additional capital into exploration, production and gas development. Crude theft nevertheless remains a major obstacle. Illegal tapping of pipelines can cause environmental damage as well as financial losses. Oil spills associated with damaged infrastructure can contaminate farmland, waterways and fishing areas, affecting communities that depend on those resources for their livelihoods. Cleaning up affected areas can be expensive and time-consuming. Community relations are therefore an important part of efforts to improve security in the Niger Delta. Residents have often complained that they receive insufficient economic benefits from the petroleum resources extracted from their communities, while also bearing the environmental consequences of oil production. Government and industry efforts to reduce theft have consequently included calls for greater community participation and development. Nigeria is also seeking to increase gas production and utilisation. Natural gas provides opportunities for electricity generation, industrial development and exports, and greater use of domestic gas could reduce some of the country's dependence on imported fuels. Investment in gas infrastructure can therefore complement efforts to increase crude production. International oil prices remain another important factor in Nigeria's economic outlook. Higher prices can increase export earnings when production is strong, but they can also raise fuel costs and inflationary pressure in countries that import refined petroleum products. Nigeria has increased domestic refining capacity and encouraged investment in refining as part of efforts to reduce its dependence on imported fuel. A stronger domestic petroleum industry could eventually retain more value within the Nigerian economy. For the government, the immediate objective is to ensure that more of the country's crude reaches legitimate production and export channels. Reducing theft and vandalism would improve revenue without necessarily requiring higher tax rates or additional borrowing. It could also improve investor confidence and support economic activity in oil-producing regions. Sustaining higher production will require continued cooperation between government agencies, security forces, oil companies and local communities. Authorities will also need to address the broader conditions that allow illegal oil operations to thrive. Employment opportunities, environmental remediation and community development can contribute to reducing incentives for criminal activity. Nigeria's efforts to increase oil output therefore form part of a wider economic strategy. Higher production can strengthen public finances and foreign-exchange supply, but long-term economic resilience will still depend on diversification beyond crude oil. For now, restoring production and reducing losses from theft remain important priorities as the government seeks to stabilise the economy and strengthen the country's external position.
img: Oil production workers and security personnel inspecting petroleum infrastructure in Nigeria's Niger Delta region.
source: Nigerian Upstream Regulatory Commission; NNPC Limited

headline: African Countries Face Growing Pressure to Prepare for Extreme Weather, AfDB Warns
summary: The African Development Bank warned that extreme weather events are creating growing economic and humanitarian risks across the continent. The bank called for stronger investment in climate resilience, early-warning systems and infrastructure capable of withstanding severe weather.
fullStory: ABIDJAN — African countries face growing economic and humanitarian risks from extreme weather and will need stronger investment in climate resilience, infrastructure and early-warning systems, according to the African Development Bank. The warning comes as governments across the continent continue to deal with the effects of droughts, floods and other weather-related emergencies. Africa remains particularly vulnerable to climate shocks because many communities depend heavily on agriculture and have limited resources for responding to major disasters. When severe drought or flooding damages crops, the effects can extend beyond farmers to food markets, transport networks and household incomes. Governments may also be forced to divert scarce resources toward emergency assistance and reconstruction. The African Development Bank has repeatedly called for greater investment in adaptation. Such investment includes improving irrigation, strengthening drainage systems, protecting water supplies and developing agricultural practices that are better suited to changing weather patterns. Early-warning systems are another important component because timely information can allow authorities and communities to prepare for extreme events and evacuate vulnerable areas before conditions become dangerous. Flooding is among the most serious risks facing many African cities and rural communities. Rapid urbanisation has increased the number of people living in areas vulnerable to flooding, while inadequate drainage and poorly planned development can worsen the impact of heavy rainfall. Roads, bridges, schools and health facilities can also be damaged when floodwaters rise rapidly. Drought creates a different set of challenges. Farmers can lose crops and livestock when rainfall falls below normal levels, while communities that depend on groundwater or surface water can face shortages. Prolonged drought can increase food insecurity and force families to migrate in search of water and livelihoods. Countries affected by conflict face additional difficulties because insecurity can prevent humanitarian organisations from reaching vulnerable communities and limit the ability of governments to invest in resilience. Climate shocks can also increase existing social pressures by reducing employment and household incomes. Agriculture is particularly important to African economies. Millions of people depend on farming either directly or indirectly, and disruptions to production can have significant effects on national economies. Lower harvests can reduce export earnings for agricultural commodities while increasing domestic food prices. Governments may then need to increase food imports or provide emergency support to affected households. The economic impact can therefore extend well beyond the communities directly affected by a weather event. The bank has argued that climate adaptation should be integrated into development planning rather than treated solely as an emergency response. New roads, bridges, housing developments and public facilities can be designed to withstand the weather conditions expected in the areas where they are built. Existing infrastructure can also be upgraded to reduce vulnerability. Financial resources remain a major obstacle. Many African countries have limited fiscal space and high debt burdens, making it difficult to finance large-scale adaptation projects without international assistance. Development institutions and international climate funds therefore have an important role to play in providing affordable financing and technical support. Private investment can also contribute, particularly in areas such as renewable energy, resilient agriculture and water infrastructure. Climate resilience is increasingly being linked to economic development because damage from extreme weather can reduce the returns on investments and delay development projects. Protecting infrastructure can therefore help governments preserve economic gains and reduce future reconstruction costs. Communities also need access to reliable information so that households, farmers and businesses can make informed decisions. Better weather forecasts can help farmers adjust planting dates, select suitable crops and prepare for periods of unusually heavy or low rainfall. Governments can use the same information to prepare emergency services and manage water resources. The African Development Bank's warning highlights the importance of acting before disasters occur. Emergency relief remains essential when communities are affected, but preventive investment can reduce both casualties and economic losses. Building resilient infrastructure, strengthening institutions and improving public awareness can help countries respond more effectively to future shocks. For African governments, the challenge is to balance immediate development needs with the growing requirement to prepare for extreme weather. With limited resources, investment decisions must focus on measures that protect the greatest number of people and strengthen essential services. International support will remain important, but domestic planning and implementation are equally necessary. As extreme weather continues to threaten communities across Africa, climate resilience is becoming an increasingly important part of economic and public policy. The African Development Bank's call for stronger preparedness reflects the need for governments to treat adaptation as a long-term development priority rather than waiting until disasters strike.
img: African communities affected by severe flooding and extreme weather as authorities strengthen climate-resilience measures.

headline: Russia and Ukraine Trade Fresh Attacks as Diplomatic Efforts Remain Uncertain
summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged fresh attacks as fighting continued despite international efforts to encourage negotiations. The latest strikes added to concerns about civilian safety and infrastructure damage as the war entered another prolonged phase.
fullStory: KYIV — Russia and Ukraine exchanged fresh attacks as fighting continued despite diplomatic efforts aimed at finding a path toward negotiations. The latest escalation added to concerns about civilian safety and damage to critical infrastructure as the war continued to affect communities across Ukraine and the wider region. Ukrainian authorities reported attacks on several areas, while Russia also accused Ukraine of launching strikes against targets on its territory. Both sides have regularly exchanged long-range attacks involving drones and missiles, with military and civilian infrastructure among the targets. The continuing strikes demonstrate the difficulty of achieving a sustained reduction in hostilities while diplomatic contacts remain uncertain. Ukraine has repeatedly called for stronger international support and security guarantees, while Russia has maintained demands linked to territory, security arrangements and other conditions for ending the conflict. Western governments have continued to support Ukraine with military, financial and humanitarian assistance while also discussing possible diplomatic avenues. The United States and European governments have faced pressure to balance military support with efforts to prevent the conflict from escalating further. The war has also continued to affect Ukraine's civilian infrastructure. Repeated attacks on electricity facilities have created challenges for the country's energy system, particularly during periods of high demand. Damage to transport infrastructure has also disrupted the movement of goods and people. Ukrainian authorities have invested in repairing damaged facilities and protecting critical infrastructure, but repeated attacks make long-term recovery difficult. Air-defence systems remain a major part of Ukraine's strategy for protecting cities and infrastructure. Ukrainian officials have repeatedly requested additional air-defence equipment from international partners, arguing that stronger protection is necessary to reduce civilian casualties and protect essential services. Russia has also continued to develop its drone and missile capabilities and has carried out large-scale attacks against Ukrainian targets. The conflict has therefore developed into a prolonged contest involving air strikes, artillery, drones and ground operations. The human cost remains significant. Civilians continue to face the risk of death and injury when attacks reach populated areas, while millions of Ukrainians have been displaced since the beginning of the full-scale invasion. Many displaced families remain dependent on government assistance and international humanitarian support. The war has also produced wider economic consequences. Ukraine has suffered extensive damage to housing, energy infrastructure, industrial facilities and transport networks. Reconstruction is expected to require enormous financial resources, with international governments and institutions discussing how to support the country's eventual recovery. Russia has also faced economic pressure from Western sanctions, although its economy has continued to support military spending. The conflict continues to affect global food and energy markets as well. Ukraine is an important agricultural producer and exporter, while Russia is a major supplier of energy and other commodities. Disruptions to exports can therefore affect prices and supply chains beyond the immediate conflict zone. Shipping routes in the Black Sea remain strategically important for both countries and for international trade. Diplomatic efforts have continued alongside the fighting, but major disagreements remain between the two sides. Any meaningful ceasefire would require agreement on security arrangements, territorial issues and mechanisms for monitoring compliance. Previous attempts to reduce hostilities have repeatedly faced difficulties, demonstrating the complexity of the negotiations. International leaders have continued to call for an end to the war, while Ukraine has stressed that any settlement must preserve its sovereignty and security. Russia has continued to insist that its own security concerns must be addressed as part of any agreement. The latest exchange of attacks therefore underscores the gap between the battlefield and diplomacy. While governments continue to explore possible negotiations, military operations remain active and neither side has accepted the other's core conditions for a settlement. For civilians, the immediate concern remains protection from further attacks and access to essential services. Humanitarian organisations continue to provide assistance to displaced families and communities affected by the fighting. The international community also faces the challenge of maintaining support for Ukraine while managing the broader economic and security consequences of the conflict. As the war continues, diplomatic efforts remain important but uncertain. A lasting reduction in violence will ultimately require an agreement that both sides are willing to accept and capable of implementing. Until that happens, communities in Ukraine and elsewhere in the region remain exposed to the consequences of continued military escalation.

headline: Floods and Landslides Kill More Than 60 in China's Beijing Region
summary: Severe flooding and landslides in and around Beijing killed more than 60 people as torrential rainfall overwhelmed communities and forced thousands of residents to evacuate. The disaster caused widespread damage to homes, roads and other infrastructure.
fullStory: BEIJING — Severe flooding and landslides in and around Beijing have killed more than 60 people following days of torrential rainfall, according to Chinese authorities. The disaster affected several communities and forced large numbers of residents to evacuate as rivers and waterways rose rapidly and floodwaters swept through low-lying areas. The extreme weather placed significant pressure on emergency services, with rescue teams deployed to search for missing people, assist stranded residents and move vulnerable communities to safer locations. Beijing and surrounding areas experienced unusually heavy rainfall, with some locations recording exceptionally high precipitation over a short period. The intense rainfall overwhelmed drainage systems and caused rivers and streams to rise quickly. Landslides were also reported in mountainous areas, where saturated soil became unstable and collapsed onto roads and settlements. Authorities issued warnings as the weather deteriorated and ordered evacuations in areas considered particularly vulnerable to flooding and landslides. Emergency shelters were opened for residents who could not safely remain in their homes. Roads and transport links were disrupted by floodwaters and debris, making it difficult for rescue teams and residents to move between affected communities. The disaster also damaged houses and public infrastructure. Electricity and communications services were disrupted in some areas as floodwaters affected facilities and roads. Chinese authorities have extensive experience responding to extreme weather events, but the scale and intensity of the rainfall presented major challenges. Rescue personnel used boats and other equipment to reach people trapped by rising water, while emergency workers searched areas affected by landslides. Local governments also mobilised medical personnel and supplies for evacuation centres. The flooding occurred during a period when parts of China were experiencing severe summer weather. Climate scientists have warned that a warming atmosphere can increase the amount of moisture available for extreme rainfall, potentially contributing to more intense precipitation events. Individual disasters, however, require detailed analysis to determine the specific influence of climate change. For residents in the affected areas, the immediate priority was survival and recovery. Families were separated from their homes, while others searched for relatives who had been reported missing. Authorities continued to update casualty figures as rescue operations progressed, meaning the number of deaths could change as emergency workers reached previously inaccessible areas. The economic impact of the disaster is also expected to be substantial. Floods can destroy agricultural land, damage roads and bridges and disrupt businesses and supply chains. Government authorities may need to spend significant amounts on emergency assistance and reconstruction after the waters recede. Businesses in affected areas can face losses when premises are damaged or operations are suspended. Agriculture can be particularly vulnerable when heavy rainfall destroys crops or erodes farmland. China has invested heavily in flood-control infrastructure and emergency-response systems, including reservoirs, drainage networks and early-warning mechanisms. However, extreme rainfall can overwhelm even substantial infrastructure when precipitation occurs at exceptional intensity. Authorities therefore rely on a combination of engineering measures, weather forecasting, evacuation plans and public warnings to reduce casualties. The disaster also highlighted the importance of early evacuation. Moving people out of vulnerable areas before rivers rise or landslides occur can significantly reduce the risk of deaths, although evacuation itself can be difficult when weather conditions deteriorate rapidly. Emergency agencies therefore need accurate forecasts and effective communication systems to reach residents quickly. Search-and-rescue operations continued as authorities assessed the full extent of the damage. Officials urged residents to remain away from flooded roads and unstable mountainous areas because additional rainfall could trigger further flooding and landslides. The risk remains particularly high when soil is saturated and rivers are already swollen. Recovery will require cooperation among local authorities, emergency agencies and affected communities. Authorities will need to restore transport and electricity services, provide temporary accommodation for displaced residents and repair damaged infrastructure. Families who lost homes or livelihoods may also require financial and social assistance. The flooding in Beijing and surrounding areas is another reminder of the destructive potential of extreme weather in densely populated regions. While emergency preparations can reduce the loss of life, increasingly severe weather events can still cause extensive damage. For China, the immediate task is to complete rescue operations, establish the final casualty figures and begin the difficult process of recovery and reconstruction.

headline: Oil Prices Fall as China Pushes for New US-Iran Peace Talks
summary: Oil prices fell more than 4% on July 24 after reports that China was pushing to restart stalled peace talks between the United States and Iran. Despite the decline, crude remained on course for a strong weekly gain as fighting and disruption around major Middle Eastern shipping routes continued.
fullStory: LONDON — Oil prices fell more than 4% on July 24 after reports that China had begun efforts to revive stalled peace talks between the United States and Iran, offering markets some hope that the escalating conflict in the Middle East could be brought under control. Brent crude settled at $96.78 a barrel, down $3.91, or 3.88%, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude settled at $89.31, down $2.88, or 3.12%. Despite the daily declines, both benchmarks remained on course for substantial weekly gains as traders continued to assess the effect of the conflict on global energy supplies. Oil prices had risen sharply during the week after the United States and Iran exchanged missile strikes and traffic through the Strait of Hormuz fell significantly. The Strait is one of the world's most important energy shipping routes, carrying large volumes of crude oil and petroleum products from the Gulf to international markets. Any prolonged disruption to the waterway could therefore have major consequences for global energy prices and inflation. The situation was further complicated by attacks on shipping in the Red Sea by Yemen's Houthi movement. The group had declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia and threatened shipping in the region as the conflict expanded. Saudi Arabia had already been seeking alternative ways to move some of its oil because of restrictions around the Strait of Hormuz. Although vessel traffic through the strait had fallen sharply, shipping data indicated that some vessels were still moving through the waterway. Analysts therefore described the situation as a serious disruption rather than a complete blockade. The possibility of renewed negotiations between Washington and Tehran nevertheless provided some relief to energy markets. China was reported to be pushing for the resumption of peace talks, raising hopes that diplomatic efforts could prevent further military escalation. Investors responded by reducing some of the risk premium that had been built into oil prices during the week. The potential consequences of the conflict extend beyond the oil market. Higher crude prices can increase transportation and manufacturing costs, raise fuel prices and add to inflationary pressure in countries that depend heavily on imported energy. Developing economies are particularly vulnerable because higher fuel costs can place pressure on foreign-exchange reserves and government finances. Nigeria and other oil-producing countries can benefit from higher crude prices through increased export earnings, but they can also face higher domestic fuel and transportation costs if global prices remain elevated. For major oil-importing economies in Asia and Europe, sustained increases in crude prices could place additional pressure on households and businesses. Energy analysts warned that the market remained vulnerable to further increases if disruptions continued. JPMorgan analysts estimated that each additional month of supply disruption could add roughly $7 to $8 per barrel to Brent crude, potentially pushing monthly average prices toward $114 if the disruption lasted for three months. The figures illustrated the potential scale of the economic consequences if shipping through the region became more severely restricted. Other developments also contributed to uncertainty in global energy markets. Russia reported strikes against Ukrainian ports that damaged infrastructure and fuel reserves, while Kazakhstan temporarily reduced oil production after suspected drone attacks affected its main Black Sea export terminal. The combination of geopolitical conflict, attacks on shipping and disruptions to energy infrastructure created a complicated outlook for traders. Markets therefore remained focused on diplomatic developments as well as military activity. A successful resumption of US-Iran negotiations could reduce fears of a prolonged supply disruption and bring further relief to oil prices. A breakdown in diplomacy, however, could quickly restore the risk premium that had pushed crude above $100 earlier in the week. For consumers and businesses around the world, the outcome of the confrontation will have consequences well beyond the Middle East. Oil remains a fundamental input for transportation, manufacturing and many other economic activities. The July 24 decline therefore provided temporary relief but did not remove the underlying risks facing global energy markets. Traders continued to monitor the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea and diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran as they assessed whether the latest decline in crude prices represented the beginning of a sustained correction or simply a pause in a highly volatile market.

headline: Nigeria's Governors Back Coordinated Security Response as States Face Rising Threats
summary: Nigeria's state governors renewed calls for stronger cooperation between federal and state security agencies as communities across parts of the country continued to face attacks and kidnappings. The governors said improved intelligence sharing and coordinated operations were essential to protecting citizens.
fullStory: ABUJA — Nigeria's state governors have renewed calls for stronger cooperation among federal and state security agencies as authorities continue to confront attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities in different parts of the country. The governors said closer coordination, better intelligence sharing and sustained security operations were necessary to protect communities and reduce the ability of armed groups to operate. Security remains one of the most important issues facing Nigeria, with different regions experiencing different forms of violence. Parts of the North-West have faced persistent banditry and kidnapping, while communities in the North-East continue to deal with the threat posed by insurgent groups. Other parts of the country have also experienced criminal violence, communal disputes and attacks on infrastructure. The governors said state authorities needed to work closely with the federal government because many security threats cross state boundaries. Criminal groups can move between local government areas and states, making isolated operations less effective. Sharing intelligence and coordinating deployments can help security agencies track suspects and respond more quickly when attacks occur. Intelligence gathering has become particularly important in combating kidnapping. Criminal groups often operate from remote locations and rely on networks that provide information, supplies and transportation. Identifying those networks requires cooperation between law-enforcement agencies and local communities. Residents can provide valuable information about suspicious movements, but authorities must also protect informants and build public confidence. The governors also highlighted the importance of strengthening security infrastructure. Better communication equipment, mobility and surveillance capabilities can improve the ability of security personnel to respond to emergencies. In rural areas, poor road networks and difficult terrain can make it harder for security forces to reach communities quickly. Expanding patrols and improving access to affected areas can therefore contribute to prevention and response. Nigeria's security challenge has significant economic consequences. Insecurity can prevent farmers from reaching their fields, disrupt markets and discourage investment. Businesses operating in affected areas may face higher security costs, while transport operators can alter routes or reduce services when roads are considered unsafe. Prolonged insecurity can therefore reduce economic activity and worsen poverty. Agriculture is particularly vulnerable. Farmers in areas affected by attacks may abandon farmland because of fear of kidnapping or violence. Reduced cultivation can contribute to food shortages and higher prices, placing additional pressure on households already facing elevated living costs. Protecting farming communities is consequently both a security and economic priority. The federal government has continued to deploy military and police personnel against armed groups, while state governments have established local security initiatives and supported community-based intelligence networks. The effectiveness of these efforts depends partly on how well different agencies coordinate their activities. Security experts have repeatedly argued that intelligence-led operations are more effective than relying solely on large-scale deployments. The governors' renewed emphasis on cooperation reflects that approach. Rather than treating individual attacks as isolated incidents, authorities need to identify the wider networks behind them and disrupt their financing, supply chains and access to weapons. The proliferation of illegal firearms remains another major concern. Criminal groups use firearms to intimidate communities, carry out kidnappings and defend their positions. National efforts to recover and destroy illicit weapons therefore form an important part of the wider security strategy. Border management is also important because firearms and other criminal resources can move across national boundaries. Nigeria shares extensive land borders with several countries, creating challenges for monitoring illegal movement. Cooperation with neighbouring governments and regional security organisations can help authorities address cross-border crime. At the community level, public confidence remains essential. Residents are more likely to provide information when they believe security agencies will respond effectively and protect them from retaliation. Building that trust requires consistent engagement and accountability. The governors' latest position therefore reflects a broader recognition that Nigeria's security problems cannot be solved by one institution alone. Federal agencies, state governments, local authorities and communities all have roles to play. Stronger coordination can improve the use of limited resources and help authorities respond more quickly to emerging threats. For Nigerians living in affected communities, the priority remains simple: greater safety and the freedom to conduct normal economic and social activities without fear. Achieving that will require sustained security operations, better intelligence, stronger institutions and attention to the economic conditions that allow criminal networks to recruit and operate. The renewed call for coordinated action is therefore an important part of the continuing national effort to improve security across Nigeria.

headline: One Killed in Lagos-Ibadan Expressway Crash as Multiple Accidents Cause Gridlock
summary: A physically challenged man was killed in a multiple-vehicle crash on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, with the incident adding to severe traffic disruption along the busy corridor. Authorities and motorists faced further congestion as several crashes affected movement around the Kara Bridge area.
fullStory: LAGOS — A physically challenged man was killed in a multiple-vehicle crash on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway, adding to a series of road incidents that caused severe congestion along the busy corridor. The crash was reported around the Kara Bridge area, one of the most heavily trafficked sections of the expressway linking Lagos with Ogun State and other parts of southwestern Nigeria. The incident occurred as motorists were already dealing with disruption caused by other crashes along the route. Emergency and traffic-management personnel were deployed to affected areas to manage the situation and assist those involved. The repeated crashes created significant delays for motorists travelling between Lagos and communities in Ogun State. The Lagos-Ibadan Expressway is a major transport route used daily by private motorists, commercial buses, trucks and other heavy vehicles. Congestion on the corridor can quickly spread to adjoining roads, particularly around the Kara Bridge and Berger areas. Road users have repeatedly raised concerns about accidents involving articulated vehicles, poor traffic management and difficult driving conditions along sections of the highway. Preliminary reports on the latest incident indicated that the victim was a physically challenged man who was on or near the highway when the crash occurred. Details surrounding the exact circumstances of the collision were still being investigated. Authorities generally advise motorists to reduce speed and maintain safe distances when approaching congested sections of the expressway because sudden stops can increase the risk of collisions. The presence of heavy trucks also creates additional dangers when vehicles lose control or suffer mechanical failures. Traffic officials have continued to work with emergency responders to clear damaged vehicles and restore the flow of traffic after major crashes. Clearing accident scenes quickly is important because disabled vehicles can block lanes and cause secondary collisions as approaching motorists attempt to manoeuvre around them. The latest incident also renewed concerns about pedestrian safety on major highways. People who walk along or cross busy expressways are particularly vulnerable because of the speed and volume of traffic. Authorities have repeatedly urged pedestrians to use designated crossing points and avoid entering carriageways where possible. Road safety remains a major public concern in Nigeria, where crashes continue to cause deaths and serious injuries. Factors contributing to road accidents can include speeding, dangerous overtaking, vehicle defects, fatigue, poor road conditions and failure to obey traffic rules. Commercial and heavy-vehicle operators face particular pressure because long-distance journeys can involve extended driving hours. The authorities' response to the latest crash therefore goes beyond clearing the immediate obstruction. Investigators are expected to establish what caused the collision and determine whether any traffic or vehicle-safety violations were involved. Such findings can help guide enforcement and prevention measures. The incident occurred against the wider backdrop of continuing efforts to improve safety on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. The Federal Government has undertaken rehabilitation and maintenance projects along the route, while traffic agencies have increased monitoring of some of the corridor's busiest sections. Despite those measures, the volume of traffic means that accidents can still have significant consequences. For commuters, the immediate effect of the latest crashes was prolonged travel time and uncertainty. Commercial drivers and businesses that depend on the highway can also suffer financial losses when vehicles remain trapped in traffic for hours. Delays can affect deliveries, passenger schedules and the movement of agricultural and industrial goods between Lagos and other parts of the country. The fatality from the latest crash underscores the human cost of road accidents. While traffic authorities can work to reduce congestion and improve enforcement, safer driving practices by motorists remain essential. Vehicle owners also have a responsibility to ensure that their vehicles are properly maintained before undertaking journeys. The authorities' investigation into the incident is expected to provide more information about the circumstances that led to the death. Meanwhile, emergency agencies continue to respond to crashes and other incidents along the expressway as they work to keep one of Nigeria's most important transport corridors open and safe for road users.

headline: Africa Could Face Up to $20 Billion Economic Loss From El Nino, AfDB Warns
summary: Africa could suffer economic losses of between $10 billion and $20 billion from an expected severe El Nino event, according to the African Development Bank's climate chief. The weather pattern could worsen droughts, floods and storms while threatening food and water security across the continent.
fullStory: ABIDJAN — Africa could face economic losses of between $10 billion and $20 billion from an expected severe El Nino event, according to Anthony Nyong, the African Development Bank's climate chief. The warning comes as countries across the continent prepare for the potential effects of a weather pattern that could produce widespread droughts, floods and storms, placing additional pressure on food production, water supplies and public finances. El Nino is a climate pattern associated with unusually warm ocean temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific. Its effects can extend far beyond the Pacific region, altering rainfall and temperature patterns in different parts of the world. For Africa, the consequences can vary between regions, with some areas experiencing severe drought while others face heavier rainfall and flooding. Nyong said the projected economic impact could be significant because many African economies remain heavily dependent on agriculture and are vulnerable to extreme weather. Farmers can lose crops and livestock when droughts reduce water availability, while floods can destroy farms, roads, homes and other infrastructure. The resulting disruption can increase food prices and place additional pressure on governments already dealing with limited fiscal resources. Africa experienced a major El Nino-related shock during 2023 and 2024, when drought and other extreme weather events caused substantial agricultural losses in several countries. Farmers lost income and food prices increased in affected markets. The African Development Bank has warned that another severe event could compound those existing pressures if governments and communities are not adequately prepared. Nigeria is among the African countries that could experience significant consequences from changing weather conditions. Agriculture remains an important source of employment and income for millions of Nigerians, particularly in rural communities. Disruptions to rainfall patterns can affect planting seasons, crop yields and livestock production, with potential consequences for food prices and household incomes. Other parts of Africa face different risks. Countries already affected by conflict and displacement may find it particularly difficult to respond to drought or flooding because their public institutions and infrastructure are under additional strain. Sudan and the Democratic Republic of Congo are among the countries identified as potentially vulnerable to the combined effects of climate shocks and existing humanitarian pressures. Severe weather can also affect government finances. Authorities may have to redirect funds toward emergency food assistance, rebuilding damaged roads and public facilities, supporting farmers and responding to displacement. Banks and businesses can also be affected when agricultural borrowers are unable to repay loans following crop failures. The economic consequences can therefore extend well beyond the immediate damage caused by a storm or drought. The African Development Bank is preparing for the possibility of greater demand for climate financing and adaptation support. Nyong said African countries could require substantial additional resources to deal with climate-related pressures and strengthen resilience. International climate funds and development partners are expected to play an important role because many vulnerable countries have limited domestic resources for large-scale adaptation projects. Preparing before extreme weather occurs can reduce the eventual cost of disasters. Measures such as improving irrigation systems, strengthening flood defences, protecting water supplies, developing climate-resilient crops and improving early-warning systems can help communities respond more effectively. Better weather forecasting can also allow farmers and governments to make decisions before conditions deteriorate. The potential economic impact of the next El Nino therefore highlights the importance of investing in resilience rather than relying solely on emergency responses after disasters occur. For African countries, this is particularly important because climate shocks can undermine development gains and increase poverty when communities lose homes, crops and sources of income. The African Development Bank's warning provides an early indication of the scale of the challenge governments could face if the forecast severe weather pattern develops. With adequate preparation, some of the potential losses can be reduced, but governments will need resources and coordination to protect vulnerable communities. The coming months will therefore be important for strengthening early-warning systems, supporting farmers and preparing infrastructure for extreme weather. For a continent already facing economic and humanitarian pressures, limiting the impact of another major climate shock will require both domestic action and international financial support.
img: African farmers working in fields affected by changing rainfall patterns, illustrating the continent's vulnerability to severe El Nino-related weather conditions.

headline: Federal Government Begins Fresh Count of Nigeria's Out-of-School Children
summary: The Federal Government has begun a nationwide exercise to establish an updated and reliable figure for children who are out of school across Nigeria. Education officials say the exercise is intended to provide evidence for better planning and targeted interventions.
fullStory: ABUJA — The Federal Government has commenced a fresh nationwide exercise to determine the number of Nigerian children currently out of school, as the Ministry of Education seeks more reliable data for planning and implementing education programmes. The exercise is aimed at addressing longstanding concerns about the accuracy and usefulness of existing estimates of Nigeria's out-of-school population. Education Minister Tunji Alausa said the government needed dependable data to understand the scale and distribution of the problem and to design interventions that respond to the circumstances of affected communities. Nigeria has one of the world's largest populations of children and has faced persistent challenges in ensuring that all school-age children have access to basic education. The reasons children remain outside the formal education system vary between communities and regions. Poverty, insecurity, distance from schools, inadequate infrastructure and social factors can all affect school attendance. In some areas, attacks and displacement have also disrupted education and forced families to move away from their communities. A reliable national count is therefore important because the number and location of out-of-school children can change as populations move and as schools open, close or become inaccessible. Education authorities need accurate information to determine where additional classrooms, teachers, learning materials and other resources are most urgently required. The new exercise is expected to provide information that can be used by federal and state governments when allocating resources. State governments are particularly important because basic education is delivered largely through state and local institutions. Accurate local data can help authorities identify communities where children are missing from school and determine the reasons for their absence. Such information can then guide targeted programmes rather than relying entirely on broad national estimates. The government has also been working with development partners and education stakeholders on measures intended to improve access to schooling. These include efforts to strengthen basic education infrastructure, support teachers and encourage children from vulnerable households to remain in school. However, officials have acknowledged that effective intervention requires reliable information about the people the programmes are intended to serve. The exercise comes against the background of Nigeria's wider efforts to improve education outcomes. The country has a large and youthful population, making education important not only for individual development but also for future economic growth. Children who remain outside school for long periods can face reduced employment opportunities later in life, while communities with low educational participation can experience wider social and economic disadvantages. Insecurity remains a particular challenge in some parts of the country. Schools in areas affected by armed conflict and criminal attacks have sometimes been closed or disrupted, while parents may be reluctant to send children to distant schools when travelling is considered unsafe. Displacement can also interrupt children's education because families may move to locations where they have limited access to formal schooling. Poverty is another significant factor. Families facing severe financial pressure may struggle to meet the indirect costs associated with education, even when tuition in public primary schools is not charged. Transport, uniforms, books and other requirements can create barriers for households with limited income. Children may also be expected to contribute to household work or income-generating activities. Addressing these challenges will require more than simply increasing school capacity. Education authorities need policies that respond to the specific reasons children are absent from school. In some communities, this may mean building schools closer to where families live. In others, authorities may need to address security concerns, provide learning materials or introduce programmes that reduce the economic burden on vulnerable families. The new national count is expected to help identify those differences. The government will also need to ensure that the data remains current after the exercise is completed. Population movements and changing economic conditions can quickly alter school attendance patterns, particularly in communities affected by displacement or insecurity. Regular data collection can therefore help education authorities adjust their programmes as circumstances change. The exercise represents an important step toward evidence-based education planning. Establishing a credible picture of Nigeria's out-of-school population can help governments and development partners direct limited resources to the areas of greatest need. The eventual success of the initiative, however, will depend on how effectively the information collected is translated into additional school places, better learning conditions and measures that help children remain in education.
source: Federal Ministry of Education; Punch Newspapers

headline: Nigeria's Naira Strengthens as Foreign-Exchange Market Sees Improved Dollar Supply
summary: The naira strengthened in Nigeria's foreign-exchange market as improved dollar liquidity supported trading conditions. The development offered some relief to businesses and importers that have faced elevated costs from currency volatility.
fullStory: ABUJA — The naira strengthened in Nigeria's foreign-exchange market as improved dollar liquidity supported trading conditions, offering some relief to businesses and importers that have faced elevated costs from currency volatility. The movement came amid the Central Bank of Nigeria's continuing efforts to improve the functioning of the foreign-exchange market and strengthen confidence in the currency. Foreign-exchange availability has been a major issue for Nigeria's economy since the government introduced significant reforms to the currency market. The reforms were designed to reduce distortions between official and unofficial exchange rates and allow market forces to play a greater role in determining the value of the naira. The adjustment initially produced substantial volatility as businesses and consumers adapted to a weaker currency. A more stable exchange rate is important for Nigerian businesses because many companies depend on imported machinery, raw materials, equipment and other inputs. When the naira loses value, the local cost of those imports rises, increasing operating expenses and often feeding into consumer prices. Importers therefore closely monitor movements in the foreign-exchange market when planning purchases and setting prices. Greater dollar liquidity can help reduce some of that uncertainty. The Central Bank has used a combination of monetary measures and market interventions to improve liquidity and strengthen confidence in the foreign-exchange market. Authorities have also worked to increase transparency and reduce opportunities for manipulation. The effectiveness of those measures depends on the availability of foreign currency from exports, investment and other legitimate sources. Nigeria's oil industry remains particularly important because crude exports generate a large share of the country's foreign-exchange earnings. Higher oil production and stronger export receipts can increase the supply of dollars available to the economy. The government has therefore placed considerable emphasis on restoring crude production after years of losses caused by theft, vandalism and operational difficulties. Non-oil exports are also important to the long-term stability of the currency. Expanding agriculture, manufacturing and services can provide additional sources of foreign exchange and reduce the economy's dependence on crude oil. The government has encouraged exporters to bring foreign-exchange proceeds into the formal market as part of efforts to strengthen supply. Remittances from Nigerians living abroad provide another important source of foreign currency. Millions of Nigerians receive funds from relatives and other contacts overseas, and the formal processing of those inflows can contribute to liquidity in the domestic market. Financial institutions have therefore been encouraged to make official channels more attractive and efficient. The movement of the naira also has implications for inflation. Nigeria has experienced substantial increases in consumer prices in recent years, with food, transportation and imported goods among the areas affected by higher costs. A more stable currency can reduce the pace at which imported inflation feeds into domestic prices, although exchange-rate stability alone cannot resolve the country's broader inflation problem. Businesses still face high energy, transportation and financing costs. The government has continued to argue that the foreign-exchange reforms will produce stronger economic conditions over time. Supporters say the previous system created distortions and discouraged investment by making it difficult for businesses to obtain foreign currency at predictable rates. Critics have pointed to the immediate economic pain caused by the adjustment and called for stronger measures to protect households and small businesses. The latest movement in the naira therefore needs to be viewed within the broader reform process rather than as a final indication of long-term currency stability. Sustained improvement will depend on stronger foreign-exchange supply, disciplined monetary policy and increased confidence among investors and businesses. Higher oil production, growing non-oil exports and increased formal remittance inflows could all support that objective. For consumers and companies, the immediate benefit of improved currency stability would be greater predictability when planning expenses and investments. For the government, a more orderly foreign-exchange market could strengthen investor confidence and support economic planning. The Central Bank will nevertheless face continued pressure to maintain liquidity while balancing exchange-rate objectives against inflation and other economic priorities. Nigeria's currency market remains closely linked to developments in oil production, global energy prices, capital flows and domestic economic policy. The recent strengthening of the naira provides some relief, but maintaining that improvement will require sustained progress across those areas.

headline: Gunmen Abduct Kebbi High Court Judge as Security Agencies Launch Rescue Operation
summary: Suspected gunmen abducted Justice Faruku Hassan Bunza of the Kebbi State High Court from his residence in Bunza Local Government Area. Police and other security agencies launched a coordinated operation to locate and rescue the judge.
fullStory: BIRNIN KEBBI — Suspected gunmen have abducted Justice Faruku Hassan Bunza, a judge of the Kebbi State High Court, from his residence in Bunza Local Government Area, prompting a coordinated security operation to secure his release. The incident occurred around midnight on Sunday, July 26, shortly after the judge returned to his residence following a trip to neighbouring Sokoto State. According to reports from the judge's family and local officials, the attackers invaded the residence along Zogirma Road and took him away. Other occupants of the house were not physically harmed during the operation. The abduction was immediately reported to the relevant authorities, including the management of the Kebbi State High Court. The incident has generated concern within the legal community because the victim is a serving judicial officer and the attack occurred at his private residence. The Kebbi State Police Command confirmed the abduction and said tactical and intelligence personnel had been deployed to locate the judge. Police Commissioner Umar Muhammad Hadejia directed security operatives to intensify efforts to find the abductors and secure Bunza's safe release. Personnel were deployed to identified locations and surrounding forest areas as investigators attempted to establish the movements of the attackers after the abduction. The Nigerian Bar Association condemned the incident, describing the abduction as an attack on the judiciary and the administration of justice. The association called for the immediate and unconditional release of the judge and urged the Kebbi State Government to work closely with federal security agencies. It also called for stronger security arrangements for judicial officers across Nigeria, noting that judges must be able to carry out their constitutional responsibilities without being exposed to threats from criminal groups. The incident adds to wider concerns about insecurity in parts of north-western Nigeria, where armed groups have carried out kidnappings, attacks on rural communities and other criminal activities. Kebbi shares borders with areas that have experienced persistent banditry, creating security challenges for communities and government institutions. Kidnapping has also increasingly affected professionals and public officials, demonstrating the ability of criminal groups to target individuals beyond rural farming communities. Security agencies face significant challenges when responding to such incidents. Criminal groups often operate in difficult terrain and can move victims between locations, making rapid intelligence gathering essential. Authorities rely on information from local communities, surveillance operations and intelligence networks to identify possible hideouts and track the movements of abductors. The police said efforts were continuing to locate the judge and bring those responsible to justice. The authorities did not initially identify a group responsible for the abduction. Reports later indicated that the kidnappers had demanded a ransom, although the circumstances surrounding the demand remained part of the ongoing investigation. The police maintained that their priority was to secure Bunza's safe return. The incident has also renewed discussion about the security of judicial officers. Judges handle sensitive cases involving criminal defendants, property disputes, political matters and other issues that can sometimes generate hostility. Protecting members of the judiciary is therefore considered important not only for individual safety but also for maintaining confidence in the justice system. Legal practitioners have repeatedly called for stronger security around courts and for judicial officers working in areas affected by insecurity. For the Kebbi State judiciary, the immediate concern remains the safe return of Justice Bunza. The police and other security agencies are expected to continue their search while investigators work to identify the perpetrators and establish how the operation was carried out. The abduction highlights the continuing security challenges facing northern Nigeria and the need for coordinated action against kidnapping networks. It also places renewed attention on the protection of public officials and judicial officers whose work is essential to the rule of law. As the rescue operation continues, authorities face pressure to secure the judge's release while ensuring that those responsible for the attack are identified and prosecuted.
