The agreement, announced on August 4, covers the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League and UEFA Conference League from the middle of 2027 through 2031. Canal+ said the arrangement would give viewers in French-speaking African countries access to all three competitions, including the Europa League and Conference League alongside the Champions League. The company already operates extensively across the African pay-TV market and has retained its existing exclusive rights in English- and Portuguese-speaking countries through its affiliate SuperSport. The agreement is significant for the African sports broadcasting market because European club football attracts a large audience across the continent. The Champions League in particular has a substantial following among African football supporters, many of whom closely follow leading European clubs and African players competing abroad. By securing the rights across a large group of countries, Canal+ is strengthening its position in the region's competitive television and streaming market. The agreement also illustrates the commercial value of football broadcasting rights. European club competitions generate substantial global audiences, making television and digital rights an important source of revenue for broadcasters and football organisations. For Canal+, securing the package provides access to premium sports content that can help retain subscribers and attract new customers. For UEFA, the agreement provides a distribution network capable of reaching millions of viewers across a rapidly developing media market. The deal also has implications for viewers. Broadcasting rights determine which platforms can legally show major sporting competitions in individual territories. The new arrangement will therefore shape how fans in Sub-Saharan Africa access UEFA matches once the agreement begins in 2027. The inclusion of the Europa League and Conference League alongside the Champions League is particularly significant for French-speaking markets, where viewers will gain access to a broader range of European club football. Canal+ said its existing arrangement with SuperSport would continue to cover English- and Portuguese-speaking markets. This means the broadcaster's regional strategy will operate through different distribution arrangements depending on language and territory. The African pay-TV industry has undergone considerable changes as broadcasters respond to competition from streaming platforms and changing consumer viewing habits. Sports content remains one of the strongest attractions for subscription television because live matches are difficult for viewers to replace with on-demand entertainment. Exclusive rights can therefore be an important part of a broadcaster's strategy. The new UEFA agreement will not take effect immediately. Current broadcasting arrangements remain in place until the new rights period begins in mid-2027. This gives broadcasters and distributors time to prepare for the transition and determine how the competitions will be offered to subscribers in individual markets. For football supporters, the development provides clarity about the future distribution of UEFA's leading club competitions in a large part of the African market. It also reinforces the importance of Sub-Saharan Africa as a commercial market for international sports organisations and media companies. The agreement is expected to strengthen Canal+'s position in African sports broadcasting while giving UEFA a major distribution partner for its club competitions. As African audiences increasingly consume sports through a combination of television, mobile devices and digital platforms, competition for premium sports rights is likely to remain strong. The Canal+ agreement therefore represents not only a broadcasting deal but also another indication of the growing commercial importance of Africa's sports media market.

headline: ECOWAS Launches Programme to Support Youth and Women Entrepreneurs
summary: The Economic Community of West African States has officially launched a regional entrepreneurship programme targeting young people and women across member states. The initiative is intended to improve access to opportunities and strengthen private-sector participation in regional economic development.
fullStory: ABUJA — The Economic Community of West African States has launched a regional entrepreneurship programme designed to support young people and women across West Africa. The programme, known as the Youth and Women Entrepreneurship Programme, was officially launched on August 4, 2026, as part of wider efforts to strengthen economic participation and regional integration. The initiative is aimed at addressing some of the barriers that young entrepreneurs and women-owned businesses face when trying to establish and expand enterprises. Access to finance, business development support, markets, skills and regional networks remains a challenge for many small businesses across West Africa. ECOWAS said the new programme would contribute to creating greater opportunities for these groups while supporting the development of the regional private sector. The initiative comes as West African governments continue to seek ways of creating jobs for a rapidly growing young population. Youth unemployment and underemployment remain important economic and social concerns in several countries, while many young people work in informal activities with limited access to formal financing and business support. Women entrepreneurs also face challenges accessing capital, markets and business networks. By focusing on both groups, the ECOWAS programme is intended to support a broader base of entrepreneurs and strengthen their participation in economic activity. Regional programmes can also help businesses look beyond their domestic markets. ECOWAS has long promoted regional integration and the movement of goods and services among member states. Entrepreneurs who are able to access neighbouring markets can potentially increase their customer base and develop larger businesses. However, differences in regulations, infrastructure, customs procedures and access to finance can make cross-border trade difficult for smaller enterprises. Support programmes therefore have the potential to help entrepreneurs overcome some of these barriers. The launch also comes amid wider efforts by ECOWAS to strengthen regional economic cooperation following significant political changes within West Africa. The withdrawal of Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger from the bloc has created new challenges for regional integration and cooperation, making programmes that strengthen economic links among remaining member states particularly significant. ECOWAS has continued to emphasise the importance of maintaining economic ties across the wider West African region. The entrepreneurship initiative is expected to involve cooperation among government institutions, private-sector organisations and other development stakeholders. Its effectiveness will depend on how programmes are implemented at national and local levels and whether intended beneficiaries can access the support available. Clear eligibility requirements, transparent selection processes and effective monitoring will be important to ensuring that assistance reaches genuine entrepreneurs. For young people, access to entrepreneurship support can provide an alternative pathway to employment and help turn business ideas into sustainable enterprises. For women, improved access to finance and markets can strengthen household incomes and increase their contribution to local and regional economies. Small and medium-sized enterprises also play an important role in job creation and domestic production across West Africa. The ECOWAS programme therefore has objectives that extend beyond individual businesses. If implemented effectively, it could contribute to stronger entrepreneurship ecosystems and greater economic participation among two groups that represent a large share of the region's population. The launch marks another step in ECOWAS's efforts to deepen regional economic cooperation and promote inclusive development. The focus will now shift to implementation and ensuring that entrepreneurs across member states can translate the programme's opportunities into sustainable businesses and jobs.

headline: Tinubu Approves Up to 80% Salary Increase for Nigerian Military Personnel
summary: President Bola Tinubu has approved salary increases of up to 80 per cent for members of Nigeria's armed forces, with the new rates scheduled to take effect from September 1. The measure is aimed at improving troop welfare and morale as the military continues to confront insurgency, banditry and kidnapping.
fullStory: ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has approved a new salary structure for Nigeria's armed forces that will increase military pay by as much as 80 per cent from September 1, 2026. The decision was announced by the Presidency as the government seeks to improve the welfare and morale of military personnel facing persistent security challenges across the country. Under the approved structure, personnel from the rank of private to staff sergeant will receive an 80 per cent salary increase, while warrant officers through colonels will receive a 50 per cent increase. Generals will receive a 30 per cent increase. The adjustment is expected to raise the annual military wage bill from about N660 billion to N924 billion. The government said the improved remuneration was intended to strengthen troop morale and support the effectiveness of the armed forces. Nigerian soldiers are deployed across several parts of the country to confront different security threats, including Islamist insurgencies in the North-East, banditry and kidnapping in the North-West and North-Central regions, as well as separatist-linked violence in parts of the South-East. The scale of the new salary increase reflects the government's effort to address the demands placed on military personnel operating in difficult and sometimes dangerous conditions. Welfare has remained an important issue in discussions about Nigeria's security sector. Personnel deployed for extended periods can face difficult living and operational conditions, while the effectiveness of military operations depends not only on equipment and training but also on the motivation and welfare of personnel. The government has also linked improved remuneration to its broader programme of military modernisation. Nigeria has increased security spending in recent years as armed groups and criminal networks have continued to operate in different parts of the country. Despite increased deployments and military operations, insecurity remains a major challenge, particularly in rural communities vulnerable to attacks and kidnappings. The new pay structure therefore comes as part of a wider security response rather than as a standalone measure. The government is expected to continue investing in equipment, training, intelligence and operational capacity alongside personnel welfare. A stronger welfare package could also help the armed forces attract and retain personnel in a highly demanding profession. However, the salary increase will add significantly to recurrent government expenditure. The annual wage bill is expected to rise by N264 billion under the new structure, meaning the government will need to accommodate the additional cost within the national budget. The measure therefore carries both security and fiscal implications. President Tinubu's approval signals that the government considers military welfare a central component of its security strategy. For personnel, the new pay structure is expected to provide immediate financial relief once implemented. For the government, the challenge will be ensuring that improved remuneration is accompanied by effective operational reforms and measurable improvements in security. The new salaries are scheduled to take effect on September 1, giving relevant government agencies time to implement the revised structure. Authorities will also be expected to ensure that the additional funding reaches eligible personnel transparently and without administrative delays. The decision marks one of the most significant recent adjustments to military remuneration in Nigeria and comes at a time when the armed forces remain heavily engaged in operations against multiple security threats.

headline: Dangote Refinery Cuts Petrol Price to N1,165 Per Litre
summary: Dangote Refinery has reduced its ex-depot petrol price to N1,165 per litre and diesel to N1,570 per litre. The company said the adjustment reflected developments in the international oil market and was intended to support consumers and businesses.
fullStory: LAGOS — Dangote Refinery has reduced the ex-depot price of petrol to N1,165 per litre and diesel to N1,570 per litre, according to reports published on August 5, 2026. The price adjustment places the refinery's latest petrol price among the key developments in Nigeria's downstream petroleum market as consumers and businesses continue to monitor fuel costs. The reduction affects the ex-depot price, which is the price at which petroleum products are sold to distributors before transportation and other downstream costs are added. The final amount paid by motorists at filling stations can therefore vary depending on location, logistics expenses and the pricing decisions of individual retailers. The refinery also reduced its diesel price to N1,570 per litre. Diesel remains an important fuel for businesses that operate generators, trucks, machinery and other equipment, particularly in areas where electricity supply is unreliable. A reduction in diesel costs can therefore lower operating expenses for transport operators, manufacturers, traders and other businesses. Dangote Refinery has increasingly become an important supplier in Nigeria's domestic petroleum market since beginning commercial operations. Its large-scale production capacity has changed the structure of the country's fuel supply system, which previously depended heavily on imported refined petroleum products. Domestic refining can reduce the amount of foreign exchange required to import finished petroleum products, although the overall effect on pump prices also depends on crude oil prices, exchange rates, transportation costs, taxes and other market factors. The latest reduction comes as petroleum prices remain closely watched by Nigerian households and businesses. Fuel prices have a direct effect on transportation and can influence the cost of food and other goods because businesses generally pass some logistics and operating costs through their prices. Diesel prices are particularly important for commercial operators that depend on private power generation. Lower diesel costs can provide some relief for such businesses if the reduction is sustained. The refinery's pricing decisions are also influenced by international crude oil and petroleum-product markets. Changes in global oil prices can affect the cost of producing and marketing refined fuels, while movements in the naira-dollar exchange rate can influence costs associated with imported inputs and equipment. Nigeria's downstream petroleum sector has undergone significant changes since the removal of the petrol subsidy, with market participants increasingly responding to commercial conditions. Consumers have consequently become more sensitive to changes in petrol prices, while businesses closely monitor fuel costs because of their impact on transportation and production. The latest Dangote price reduction could provide short-term relief if distributors and retailers pass a meaningful portion of the reduction through to consumers. However, the actual effect on pump prices will depend on market conditions across different locations. The development also highlights the growing role of domestic refining in Nigeria's petroleum supply chain. As refinery capacity expands, policymakers and industry operators are expected to focus on ensuring that domestic production remains competitive while maintaining reliable supplies. For consumers, the immediate issue will be whether the lower ex-depot price translates into lower retail prices at filling stations. For businesses, reduced diesel costs could provide some relief from energy and transportation expenses. The latest adjustment therefore represents another significant movement in Nigeria's evolving downstream petroleum market.

headline: Nigeria's Foreign Reserves Reach $52.5bn, CBN Reports
summary: Nigeria's foreign exchange reserves rose to $52.5 billion, reaching their highest level in about 17 years, according to the Central Bank of Nigeria. The increase strengthens the country's external buffer as authorities continue implementing economic and foreign-exchange reforms.
fullStory: ABUJA — Nigeria's foreign exchange reserves have risen to $52.5 billion, reaching their highest level in about 17 years, according to figures from the Central Bank of Nigeria. The increase represents a significant improvement in the country's external position and provides the authorities with a stronger buffer against external economic pressures. Foreign exchange reserves are important to Nigeria because they provide resources that can support international payments and help strengthen confidence in the country's ability to meet external obligations. The latest increase comes as the Central Bank continues implementing reforms aimed at improving the foreign exchange market and restoring investor confidence. Nigeria's external reserves have historically been influenced by crude oil earnings, foreign investment and other capital inflows. Oil remains one of the country's major sources of foreign exchange, meaning developments in crude production and international oil prices can have a substantial effect on reserve accumulation. The stronger reserve position also comes amid efforts by the government to improve economic conditions and attract more investment. Increased foreign capital inflows can provide additional foreign exchange while supporting investment in productive sectors. However, the rise in reserves does not remove the broader economic challenges facing households and businesses. Inflation, high operating costs and foreign-exchange pressures continue to affect economic activity across the country. Analysts are therefore expected to monitor whether the improvement in reserves can be sustained over the coming months. Maintaining stronger reserves will depend on continued foreign-exchange inflows, improved oil production, non-oil exports, investment and sound macroeconomic management. The latest figure nevertheless represents a substantial improvement in Nigeria's external position and gives policymakers greater room to respond to external shocks. For businesses and investors, a stronger reserve position can also contribute to confidence in the country's financial system and its capacity to manage periods of foreign-exchange volatility. The Central Bank is expected to continue monitoring developments in the foreign exchange market while pursuing policies intended to improve liquidity and strengthen confidence. The reserve increase therefore marks an important development in Nigeria's ongoing economic adjustment, although its longer-term significance will depend on whether the country can sustain the growth in external reserves while addressing inflation and other structural economic pressures.

headline: Nigeria's Manufacturing Sector Records Stronger Growth in July
summary: Nigeria's manufacturing sector recorded stronger business activity in July as output and new orders improved, according to the latest purchasing managers' data. The improvement points to a gradual strengthening of industrial activity despite continuing cost pressures facing manufacturers.
fullStory: LAGOS — Nigeria's manufacturing sector recorded stronger business activity in July, with output and new orders improving during the month, according to the latest purchasing managers' data reported by Nigerian business news outlets. The improvement points to a gradual strengthening of industrial activity as manufacturers respond to changing economic conditions and demand. Manufacturing remains an important part of Nigeria's effort to diversify its economy away from excessive dependence on crude oil. The sector supports employment, domestic production and supply chains spanning agriculture, transportation, logistics and retail. An improvement in new orders is therefore significant because it indicates stronger demand for locally produced goods. Higher orders can encourage manufacturers to increase production, retain workers and purchase additional raw materials. However, manufacturers continue to operate under significant cost pressures. Energy expenses, transportation costs, imported inputs and foreign-exchange movements can all affect the cost of production in Nigeria. Many factories also rely partly on private power generation because of limitations in the national electricity supply. Changes in diesel prices and other energy costs can therefore have a direct effect on manufacturing margins. The July improvement comes as businesses continue to adjust to the economic reforms introduced by the Federal Government and the Central Bank of Nigeria. Changes in foreign-exchange policy and efforts to improve market liquidity have affected companies that depend on imported machinery, components and raw materials. Manufacturers have repeatedly called for policies that provide greater stability in the operating environment. Predictable access to foreign exchange, reliable electricity and efficient transportation are among the conditions businesses say are necessary for sustained industrial growth. The improvement in manufacturing activity is also relevant to employment. A sustained increase in production can support existing jobs and create additional demand for workers as companies expand capacity. It can also benefit smaller businesses that supply manufacturers with packaging, transportation, maintenance and other services. Despite the positive signals, one month of stronger activity does not necessarily indicate a permanent turnaround. Manufacturing performance can change quickly in response to consumer demand, inflation, exchange-rate movements and production costs. Businesses therefore continue to monitor economic conditions closely before making major investment decisions. The sector's longer-term performance will depend on whether stronger demand can be maintained and whether production costs become more manageable. Increased local production could also reduce Nigeria's reliance on imported goods and strengthen domestic supply chains. Government policies aimed at supporting local manufacturing have included initiatives encouraging domestic production and investment in industrial capacity. Manufacturers have also sought stronger implementation of these policies and better infrastructure to make Nigerian products more competitive. The July figures provide an encouraging signal for the sector, but industry stakeholders are likely to focus on whether the improvement continues through subsequent months. Sustained growth would strengthen the contribution of manufacturing to employment, tax revenue and economic diversification. For now, the latest data suggest that Nigerian manufacturers entered August with stronger levels of business activity than they recorded at the beginning of the previous month, even as significant operating challenges remain.

headline: Tinubu Directs Stronger Security Measures After Rescue of 308 Abductees
summary: President Bola Tinubu has directed security agencies to strengthen early-warning systems following the rescue of 308 people abducted in Kwara and Niger states. The President commended the agencies involved and called for measures to prevent future mass abductions.
fullStory: ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has directed Nigeria's security agencies to strengthen early-warning and intelligence systems following the rescue of 308 people abducted in Kwara and Niger states. The directive followed an intelligence-led operation that secured the release of the victims from the Kainji Lake National Park area. According to the Presidency, 163 of the victims were abducted from Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area of Kwara State, while another 145 were kidnapped in Niger State. The victims were recovered during a coordinated operation involving the National Counter-Terrorism Centre, the Armed Forces, the Department of State Services and the Nigeria Police Force. The Presidency described the operation as the largest single-day rescue mission undertaken by Nigeria's security agencies. Tinubu commended the personnel involved and said the successful operation demonstrated the importance of coordinated intelligence and security action. The President also directed the security agencies to improve mechanisms for detecting threats before they develop into large-scale attacks. Early-warning systems are intended to help security agencies identify movements and threats in vulnerable communities and respond before kidnappers or armed groups can carry out mass attacks. The rescue comes after months of security concerns in parts of Kwara and Niger states, where communities have faced threats from kidnapping and other forms of armed violence. Woro and surrounding communities in Kwara have previously experienced attacks that forced residents to seek stronger protection from the authorities. The recovery of the victims from the Kainji Lake National Park area also highlights the security challenge presented by large forested territories. Such areas can provide hiding places for criminal groups and make surveillance and ground operations more difficult. Security agencies have increasingly relied on intelligence-led operations, surveillance and cooperation between different agencies to locate abducted persons and disrupt criminal networks. The latest operation demonstrates the importance of such coordination, particularly where kidnappers operate across state boundaries. Following their release, the victims are expected to undergo medical assessment and receive assistance before being reunited fully with their families and communities. People who have spent extended periods in captivity can require medical and psychological support, especially where they have experienced deprivation or violence. The operation nevertheless represents only one part of the broader security challenge. Kidnapping continues to affect communities in several parts of Nigeria, and authorities face pressure to prevent attacks rather than relying primarily on rescue operations after victims have been taken. Strengthening intelligence networks, protecting vulnerable communities and disrupting the financial and logistical networks supporting kidnapping remain important elements of the national security response. The Presidency said the latest rescue should encourage security agencies to maintain pressure on criminal groups while improving preventive measures. For the affected families, the release brings relief after a prolonged period of uncertainty. For the government, however, the development also reinforces the need to ensure that communities vulnerable to mass abductions receive adequate protection and that security agencies can identify emerging threats quickly. Tinubu's directive therefore places renewed emphasis on prevention, intelligence sharing and coordinated security operations as Nigeria continues its efforts to tackle kidnapping and other forms of insecurity.

headline: Nigeria's Foreign Reserves Hit 17-Year High at $52.5bn
summary: Nigeria's foreign exchange reserves have risen to $52.5 billion, their highest level in 17 years, according to the Central Bank of Nigeria. The increase was attributed to renewed investor confidence and sustained capital inflows into the economy.
fullStory: ABUJA — Nigeria's foreign exchange reserves have risen to $52.5 billion, reaching their highest level in 17 years, according to figures disclosed by the Central Bank of Nigeria. The development was reported by Vanguard on August 5, 2026, with the apex bank attributing the increase to renewed investor confidence and sustained capital inflows into the Nigerian economy. The latest reserve position represents an important development for Nigeria because the country's foreign exchange reserves provide a buffer for meeting external obligations and supporting confidence in the economy. Foreign reserves are held in foreign currencies and other external assets and can help a country manage periods of pressure on its balance of payments and foreign exchange market. The CBN said the reserves had surpassed its annual target, indicating stronger-than-expected accumulation during the period. The increase comes after several years in which Nigeria's external reserves and foreign exchange market faced pressure from lower oil production, reduced foreign investment and difficulties accessing foreign currency. Oil remains an important source of foreign exchange for Nigeria, making crude production and international oil prices significant factors in the country's external position. However, the CBN also pointed to renewed investor confidence and capital inflows as contributors to the latest increase. Capital inflows can come through portfolio investment, foreign direct investment and other international financial transactions. Stronger inflows can provide additional foreign exchange and improve liquidity in the domestic market. The reserve increase also comes amid reforms introduced by the Federal Government and the Central Bank to improve the functioning of Nigeria's foreign exchange market. The authorities have sought to reduce distortions in the market, improve transparency and create conditions that encourage investment. A stronger reserve position can support these efforts by giving policymakers greater capacity to respond to external shocks. It can also strengthen confidence among international investors and businesses that require access to foreign currency for legitimate transactions. However, the reserve figure does not by itself resolve all of Nigeria's economic challenges. The country continues to face inflationary pressure, high operating costs and concerns about household purchasing power. The benefits of stronger external reserves will therefore depend partly on how effectively broader economic reforms translate into improved conditions for businesses and households. Nigeria's foreign exchange position is also affected by crude oil production and export earnings. Efforts to increase oil output, attract investment into the upstream petroleum sector and expand non-oil exports remain important to sustaining reserve accumulation. The government has been promoting reforms intended to improve the investment environment and attract new capital into the economy. The reported $52.5 billion reserve position provides a stronger external buffer than Nigeria has had in many years. It could help improve confidence in the country's ability to meet international obligations and withstand periods of volatility in global financial markets. Analysts will nevertheless continue to monitor the sustainability of the increase, particularly the sources of new inflows and the performance of oil and non-oil exports. Sustained reserve growth would require continued capital inflows, stronger production and exports, disciplined macroeconomic management and an improvement in investor confidence. For now, the latest CBN figure marks a significant improvement in Nigeria's external position and provides the government with greater financial room as it continues implementing economic reforms.

headline: FG Launches 13.92MW Solar Mini-Grid Project in Yobe
summary: The Federal Government has launched a 13.92-megawatt solar mini-grid project in Yobe State as part of efforts to expand electricity access and support economic activity in underserved communities. The project is expected to provide more reliable power for households, businesses and public institutions.
fullStory: DAMATURU — The Federal Government has launched a 13.92-megawatt solar mini-grid project in Yobe State as part of efforts to expand electricity access and support economic activities in communities with limited access to reliable power. The project was among developments reported in Nigeria on August 5, 2026, as the government continued to pursue alternative energy solutions alongside efforts to improve the national electricity system. The solar mini-grid is designed to provide electricity to communities that have faced limitations in access to conventional grid power. Renewable-energy projects of this type can help households, businesses, schools, health facilities and other public institutions obtain more dependable electricity without waiting for the expansion of conventional transmission and distribution infrastructure. The initiative is also significant for small businesses that depend on electricity to operate equipment, preserve goods and provide services. Reliable power can reduce the amount businesses spend on alternative sources such as petrol and diesel generators, although the actual savings will depend on tariffs, operating costs and the reliability of the new system. Yobe is one of the Nigerian states where solar power has significant potential because of its high levels of sunlight. The deployment of solar infrastructure therefore forms part of a broader strategy to use renewable energy to improve electricity access in areas where extending the national grid can be difficult or expensive. The Federal Government has increasingly promoted mini-grids and other distributed-energy systems as a way of complementing the national electricity network. Unlike large power stations that depend on extensive transmission infrastructure, mini-grids can supply defined communities or groups of users through smaller local networks. The project also comes as Nigeria continues to face electricity-supply challenges. Unreliable power has long affected households and businesses, contributing to higher operating costs and limiting productivity. For manufacturers and small enterprises, electricity shortages can increase dependence on generators and make production more expensive. In rural and underserved communities, inadequate electricity can also affect education, healthcare and access to digital services. A functioning solar mini-grid can therefore have effects beyond household lighting. It can support refrigeration, water pumping, communications, information technology and other activities that require dependable electricity. The success of the Yobe project will depend on the quality of installation, maintenance, management and the sustainability of its financing model. Solar equipment also requires regular maintenance and eventual replacement of components as they reach the end of their operating lives. Government agencies and local stakeholders will therefore need to ensure that the infrastructure remains operational after commissioning. The project is part of the wider national effort to diversify Nigeria's electricity sources and increase the role of renewable energy in the country's power mix. Solar projects have become increasingly important as Nigeria seeks solutions to persistent power shortages and the high cost of diesel and petrol-powered generation. For communities in Yobe, the immediate priority will be translating the new infrastructure into dependable electricity and productive economic activity. If properly maintained and effectively managed, the mini-grid could provide a more stable power supply for residents and businesses while contributing to the state's broader development.

headline: Security Forces Rescue 308 Abducted Persons in Kwara and Niger
summary: Security agencies have rescued 308 people abducted in separate attacks in Kwara and Niger states. President Bola Tinubu described the operation as the largest single-day rescue mission carried out by Nigeria's security agencies and ordered stronger early-warning measures against mass abductions.
fullStory: ABUJA — Nigerian security agencies have rescued 308 people abducted in separate attacks in Kwara and Niger states, in what the Presidency described as the country's largest single-day rescue operation. President Bola Tinubu welcomed the development on August 5, 2026, and directed security agencies to strengthen early-warning systems to prevent future mass abductions. According to a statement issued by the President's Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, 163 of the rescued victims were abducted from Woro community in Kaiama Local Government Area of Kwara State, while another 145 people were kidnapped in a separate attack in Niger State. The victims were rescued from the Kainji Lake National Park forest in New Bussa Local Government Area of Niger State during a coordinated intelligence-led operation. The operation involved the National Counter-Terrorism Centre, the Armed Forces, the Department of State Services and the Nigeria Police Force. The rescue represents a significant development for families and communities affected by the attacks, particularly in areas where insecurity and mass abductions have created prolonged fear. Woro and neighbouring communities in Kwara have faced serious security concerns, with residents previously calling for stronger government action following attacks and abductions. The use of the Kainji Lake National Park forest as the location where victims were recovered also highlights the continuing challenge security agencies face in areas where large forested territories can provide hiding places for criminal and armed groups. President Tinubu commended the security agencies involved in the operation and directed them to improve intelligence gathering and early-warning mechanisms. Such systems are intended to help authorities detect threats earlier and respond before attacks develop into large-scale abductions. The rescue also underscores the importance of cooperation among the military, police, intelligence agencies and other security institutions. Coordinated operations can allow agencies to combine intelligence, surveillance and operational resources when dealing with kidnappers and armed groups operating across state boundaries. For the rescued victims, attention will now turn to medical assessment, psychological support and reunification with their families. People held in captivity for extended periods can require medical and social assistance after release, particularly where they have experienced violence, deprivation or difficult living conditions. The operation also comes amid continuing efforts by the Federal Government and state authorities to address insecurity in parts of northern Nigeria. Kidnapping and terrorism have remained major concerns in several communities, with authorities under pressure to protect rural populations, travellers and vulnerable settlements. Although the rescue is a major success for the security agencies involved, it does not by itself resolve the wider threat of abduction. Preventing future attacks will require sustained intelligence operations, protection of vulnerable communities and action against the networks that finance and organise kidnapping. The Presidency said the latest operation demonstrated the capacity of Nigerian security agencies to conduct complex coordinated missions. It also emphasised the need to improve preventive measures so that security responses are not limited to rescuing victims after attacks have already occurred. As the rescued people return to their families, authorities are expected to continue investigations into the attacks and the groups responsible. The operation therefore provides immediate relief to hundreds of families while placing renewed attention on the need for stronger security and early-warning mechanisms in communities vulnerable to mass abductions.

headline: NUPRC Targets $30bn to $50bn Investment From 22 Offshore Projects
summary: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission says 22 major offshore oil and gas projects expected between 2026 and 2030 could attract between $30 billion and $50 billion in investment. The commission said the projects are expected to increase production, create jobs and strengthen Nigeria's energy security.
fullStory: LAGOS — The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission has projected between $30 billion and $50 billion in investment from 22 major offshore oil and gas projects expected to be developed between 2026 and 2030. The commission said the projects form part of efforts to increase Nigeria's crude oil production, create jobs, expand infrastructure and strengthen energy security. NUPRC Chief Executive Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan disclosed the projection at the Society of Petroleum Engineers' Nigeria Annual International Conference and Exhibition in Lagos on August 5, 2026. Eyesan was represented at the event by the commission's Executive Commissioner for Development and Production, Enorense Amadasu. According to the commission, the anticipated investments represent an important pipeline of activity for Nigeria's upstream petroleum industry. The projects are expected to support new production capacity while encouraging further investment in offshore oil and gas developments. NUPRC said it had approved more than $57 billion worth of Field Development Plans since 2024, with some of those approvals already progressing to Final Investment Decisions. A Field Development Plan outlines how an oil or gas field is expected to be developed and brought into production. The commission said Nigeria was continuing to develop its proven hydrocarbon reserves while maintaining a pipeline of exploration opportunities intended to support longer-term growth. It also pointed to successive licensing rounds conducted since 2022 as part of efforts to open access to prospective oil and gas acreage. In the 2025 licensing round, 31 companies emerged as successful bidders for 37 oil and gas blocks following an evaluation process described by the commission as data-driven and technology-enabled. NUPRC said the forthcoming 2026 licensing round was also attracting interest, with the commission highlighting transparency in recent licensing processes as a factor expected to support investor confidence. The anticipated offshore projects could have wider economic implications if the planned investments translate into actual development and production. Increased oil output could improve government revenue and export earnings, while new projects could generate employment and create demand for services across the petroleum supply chain. The commission also linked the investments to energy security, as stronger domestic production could help Nigeria maintain a more stable supply of crude for local refining and export markets. However, the projected investment figure represents expected potential rather than money already committed to all 22 projects. Actual investment will depend on project financing, commercial decisions, regulatory approvals, technical conditions and final investment decisions by the companies involved. Nigeria's oil industry has faced production challenges in recent years, including crude theft, pipeline disruptions, ageing infrastructure and difficulties attracting sufficient investment. The government has therefore placed greater emphasis on regulatory reforms and new investment in the upstream sector. The NUPRC said its licensing and development efforts were intended to create a more predictable environment for investors while ensuring that Nigeria's petroleum resources contribute more effectively to national development. If the projects proceed as projected, they could become an important source of new production and investment during the next four years. The commission said the focus would remain on translating approved development plans and licensing opportunities into actual projects, production and economic value.

headline: FG Plans Sports and Education Centres of Excellence Across Tertiary Institutions
summary: The Federal Government has unveiled a programme to establish Sports and Education Centres of Excellence in selected tertiary institutions, combining academic education with elite sports development. The initiative is intended to create structured pathways for young Nigerians to pursue both education and sporting careers.
fullStory: ABUJA — The Federal Government has unveiled a National Sports and Education Excellence Programme designed to combine academic education with elite sports development in selected Nigerian tertiary institutions. The initiative, known as N-SEEP, is being implemented jointly by the Federal Ministry of Education and the National Sports Commission. The programme will establish specialised centres where talented young Nigerians can pursue academic programmes while receiving structured sports training. The first phase is expected to involve the University of Ibadan, Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, Federal College of Education, Okene and Babcock University. Other institutions listed for subsequent phases include the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, the University of Benin, the University of Jos, Muhammad Buhari University in Maiduguri and the Federal Polytechnic, Offa. Education Minister Tunji Alausa said the programme was designed to address the longstanding challenge faced by young athletes who have had to choose between academic development and sporting careers. Under the initiative, students would be able to develop their sporting abilities while obtaining academic qualifications and professional skills. The programme is also expected to create training opportunities in areas beyond competitive sports, including sports science, coaching, sports medicine, rehabilitation, sports technology, data analytics, sports business, facility management, event management and sports administration. The National Sports Commission said it would work with participating institutions to strengthen sports infrastructure and professional training for coaches. Officials also said discussions were ongoing with international sporting organisations over possible accreditation of sports-related academic programmes. The government said the initiative would eventually extend beyond tertiary institutions, with plans for Sports Centres of Excellence in Unity Schools as well as state and private schools. The broader objective is to identify promising athletes early and provide them with a structured pathway through the education system. The programme comes amid continuing efforts to strengthen Nigeria's sports development system and reduce the loss of talented young athletes who lack access to facilities, coaching and sustainable career pathways. Officials said combining education and sports could also create opportunities in sports medicine, technology, media, administration and event management. The government said implementation would take place in phases as participating institutions prepare their facilities and programmes. The success of the initiative will depend on adequate funding, qualified personnel, appropriate facilities and transparent systems for identifying and supporting talented students.

headline: Abeokuta North Commissions Education Projects as Council Expands Grassroots Development
summary: Abeokuta North Local Government in Ogun State has commissioned development projects covering education and other sectors across its 16 wards and four major communities. The council said the projects were part of efforts to improve infrastructure and strengthen grassroots development.
fullStory:
ABEOKUTA — Abeokuta North Local Government Area of Ogun State has commissioned several development projects, including interventions in education, as the council expands its grassroots development programme across the area.

The projects, commissioned on August 7, 2026, cover the council's 16 wards and four major communities and include education, healthcare, rural electrification, potable water supply, sanitation, road infrastructure and public facilities. The development was reported by Vanguard and P.M. News. 

The commissioning was led by the Chairman of Abeokuta North Local Government, Olanrewaju Ayodeji Oyegbola-Sodipo. The Ogun State Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, Ganiyu Hamzat, also attended the event and commended the council administration for its infrastructure investments.

According to the reports, the education-related projects formed part of a wider programme aimed at improving public facilities and the quality of life of residents. The council did not, however, provide detailed information in the reports on the number of schools involved or the specific nature and cost of each education project. 

The broader infrastructure programme also included improvements involving water supply, sanitation, roads and healthcare facilities. The council said the projects reflected its focus on infrastructure renewal and human development.

Hamzat described the investments in schools, water infrastructure, sanitation facilities and council assets as part of responsive grassroots governance and said they were aligned with the development agenda of the Ogun State Government.

The education component comes as education remains an important part of Ogun State's broader development efforts. Earlier in the week, Ogun State Universal Basic Education Board, in collaboration with the Universal Basic Education Commission, launched a Farm Produce and Agricultural Science Exhibition at Imo Methodist Nursery and Primary School, Oke-Yeke, Abeokuta. The initiative was designed to strengthen practical Agricultural Science education, with SUBEB saying about 80 public primary and junior secondary schools had benefited from the programme. 

The Abeokuta North council chairman said his administration had prioritised education alongside infrastructure renewal, healthcare, youth empowerment, environmental management, institutional reforms and community security.

He also stressed the importance of public participation in the implementation of government programmes, saying sustainable development required cooperation between government and residents.

The commissioning therefore represents a broader infrastructure intervention rather than the reopening of a single education facility. The available reports do not establish that a particular school or education project was 'reopened', as stated in the original headline supplied for this record.

For residents, the impact of the education projects will depend on the quality of the facilities, their continued maintenance and how effectively they serve pupils and teachers. Stakeholders have increasingly emphasised the need for education investments to translate into safer and better-equipped learning environments.

The council's wider programme also includes infrastructure intended to improve basic services and living conditions across its communities. The combination of education, healthcare, water, sanitation and road projects reflects an attempt to address several local development needs simultaneously.

As the projects move from commissioning to use, attention is expected to shift towards maintenance, service delivery and the extent to which the facilities benefit residents. Effective implementation will be important in determining the long-term value of the investments.

The development comes amid continuing efforts by government institutions in Ogun State to strengthen basic education infrastructure and improve learning opportunities. For Abeokuta North, the newly commissioned projects provide an opportunity to translate the council's infrastructure plans into tangible improvements for communities across its wards.

headline: Ilorin Reviews Food Supply Plan as Rising Costs Put Pressure on Households
summary: Authorities and stakeholders in Ilorin reviewed measures to stabilise food supplies as rising prices continued to put pressure on households and businesses. Attention focused on improving distribution, supporting local producers and ensuring essential food items remain accessible.
fullStory:
ILORIN — Authorities and economic stakeholders in Ilorin reviewed measures to stabilise food supplies as rising prices and distribution challenges continued to put pressure on households and businesses. Residents and industry representatives called for practical steps to improve the availability and affordability of essential food items.

Food prices have remained a major concern for households as higher transportation, production and distribution costs affect the prices paid by consumers. Stakeholders said sustained pressure on household budgets could reduce the ability of families to afford adequate food and other basic necessities.

The situation has also affected traders and small businesses. Market operators face higher costs when transporting goods from farms and wholesale markets to retail outlets. Some businesses have had to adjust their prices to cover increased operating expenses while trying to retain customers.

Stakeholders said strengthening local agricultural production could help improve food security and reduce some pressures on supply. Farmers need access to affordable inputs, financing, storage facilities and reliable transportation to move their produce efficiently to markets.

Transportation was identified as a particularly important part of the food supply chain. Poor roads, higher fuel costs and other logistical challenges can increase the final price of agricultural products. Stakeholders urged authorities to improve transportation networks and address bottlenecks affecting the movement of food.

Storage was another area of concern. Inadequate storage facilities can lead to significant losses, particularly for perishable agricultural products. Stakeholders said investment in modern storage facilities could help preserve food, reduce waste and improve the stability of supplies between harvest periods.

Market operators also called for better coordination between producers, distributors and retailers. They said clearer information about supply levels and market conditions could help businesses plan purchases and reduce unnecessary disruptions.

Consumers have also been adjusting their spending patterns. Some households have reduced purchases of more expensive food items or switched to cheaper alternatives. Residents said continued increases could make it increasingly difficult for families to maintain balanced diets.

Stakeholders said support for vulnerable households should form part of broader efforts to address food insecurity. They called for targeted interventions that could assist households facing the greatest financial pressure without creating additional distortions in local markets.

The role of local farmers was also emphasised. Stakeholders said stronger connections between farmers and urban markets could create more reliable supply channels while providing producers with better access to consumers. Improved market information could also help farmers make decisions about production and pricing.

Food processors were encouraged to expand local value addition. Processing agricultural products within the region could extend shelf life, reduce losses and create employment opportunities while strengthening local supply chains.

Residents urged authorities to communicate clearly about measures being introduced to address food supply challenges. They said transparent information would help businesses and households understand available support and prepare for changes in market conditions.

As attention shifted towards implementation, stakeholders in Ilorin called for practical measures covering agricultural production, transportation, storage and market distribution. They said coordinated action would be necessary to improve food availability and reduce pressure on consumers.

The discussions highlighted the importance of building a more resilient food supply system. Stakeholders expressed hope that stronger support for producers and improvements in distribution infrastructure would help Ilorin respond to current economic pressures while preparing for future challenges.

headline: Jos Promotes Student Support Scheme as Residents Demand Faster Action
summary: Education stakeholders in Jos have called for stronger student support measures as rising economic pressures continue to affect learners and their families. Residents urged authorities and institutions to move quickly on practical assistance that can help students remain in school and complete their studies.
fullStory:
JOS — Education stakeholders in Jos have called for stronger student support measures as economic pressures continue to affect learners and their families. Residents and community representatives said practical assistance was needed to help students remain in school and reduce the financial difficulties facing households.

The cost of education has remained a concern for many families, with expenses covering tuition, learning materials, transportation, accommodation and other basic needs. Stakeholders said students from low-income households were particularly vulnerable when families struggled to meet these costs.

Community representatives said a well-structured student support scheme could help reduce some of the pressure. They called for assistance that would reach students based on clear and transparent criteria while ensuring that available resources were distributed fairly.

Stakeholders also highlighted the importance of learning materials. Students without adequate textbooks, digital devices or other educational resources can face difficulties keeping pace with their classmates. Support programmes, they said, should therefore consider both direct financial assistance and access to essential learning tools.

Digital learning has also become increasingly important in education. Students are using smartphones, computers and online platforms to access academic materials, communicate with teachers and complete assignments. However, the cost of devices, electricity and internet data can make digital learning difficult for some households.

Residents urged institutions and relevant authorities to consider these challenges when designing student support programmes. They said assistance should reflect the different circumstances of students rather than relying on a single form of intervention.

Students also called for clearer information about available support. Stakeholders said eligible beneficiaries should be able to easily understand application requirements, deadlines and the process for receiving assistance. Transparent communication could help reduce confusion and prevent students from missing opportunities.

Community leaders stressed the need for proper monitoring of support programmes. They said authorities should maintain accurate records of beneficiaries and regularly assess whether assistance was producing the intended results. Effective monitoring, they added, would also help reduce the risk of resources being diverted from their intended purpose.

Education stakeholders said student support should extend beyond financial assistance. Academic counselling, mentorship and career guidance could help students deal with academic pressures and make better decisions about their education and future employment.

The scheme could also provide opportunities for collaboration between educational institutions, government agencies, community organisations and private-sector groups. Stakeholders said partnerships could expand the resources available and allow support programmes to reach more students.

Residents maintained that timely action was important. Delays in providing assistance could leave students struggling with basic educational expenses and, in some cases, increase the risk of absenteeism or withdrawal from school.

As attention shifted towards implementation, stakeholders in Jos called for a practical and transparent student support system that would address the financial, academic and digital challenges facing learners. They said regular reviews would be necessary to ensure that the programme remained responsive to changing needs.

The discussions highlighted the importance of keeping students in education despite economic difficulties. Stakeholders expressed hope that stronger support measures would reduce barriers to learning and give more students the opportunity to complete their education successfully.
